<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/index.md -->

# VMnodes documentation

VMnodes runs web apps for a business, and these docs tell you how to build one that runs on it. Start here to find the page that matches your task.

## What VMnodes is

VMnodes is a managed runtime for software built for a small or mid-sized business. An org's administrator puts an app online from a git repository in a web portal, and VMnodes builds it, runs it at its own address and keeps it running. A gateway in front of every app signs people in and tells the app who each person is, so the app never builds a login page. VMnodes also gives each app roles, an optional database, and a way to share its records with other apps in the org.

## Who these docs are for

These docs are written for AI coding agents that build an app for a customer who is not technical, and for the people who read over the agent's shoulder. Every page says what to do and what you see when it worked, so you can tell done from not done.

## If you are an AI agent, read these in order

1. [Getting started](getting-started.md): download the starter, run it, put it online, change it.
2. [Sign-in and identity](concepts/sign-in-and-identity.md): how a request reaches your app and how your app must check who sent it.
3. [`vmnodes.json`](reference/vmnodes-json.md): the one file that declares your roles, your database and what your app shares.
4. The how-to below that matches your task.

Read the other concept pages when a task touches them: [orgs and people](concepts/orgs-and-people.md), [apps](concepts/apps.md), [roles](concepts/roles.md), [data](concepts/data.md), [sharing](concepts/sharing.md), [connectors](concepts/connectors.md).

## How-tos

| Your task | Read |
|---|---|
| Build an app where people fill in a form and see a list | [Build a form-and-list app](how-to/form-and-list.md) |
| One person submits, another approves | [Submit and approve](how-to/approvals.md) |
| Keep data when the app is updated | [Keep data through updates](how-to/keep-data-through-updates.md) |
| Share your app's records with other apps in the org, keeping some fields private | [Share data](how-to/share-data.md) |
| Read records another app shares | [Read shared data](how-to/read-shared-data.md) |
| Change an app someone else built | [Change an app](how-to/change-an-app.md) |
| Show dates, "today", overdue or this week in the business's time zone | [Dates and time zones](how-to/dates-and-time-zones.md) |
| Run the database tests on your own computer | [Test with a scratch database](how-to/test-with-a-scratch-database.md) |

When something fails, search [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md) for the exact message you saw. Facts you may need while building are in the reference pages: [environment variables](reference/environment.md), [build and run](reference/build-and-run.md), [the identity package](reference/identity-sdk.md), [the publish API](reference/publish-api.md) and [limits](reference/limits.md).

## What VMnodes does for you

- Builds your repository into a running app, from a root `Dockerfile` or from a Node project with a `package-lock.json`.
- Gives the app its own address, `<app>.<org>.vmnodes.com`, over https.
- Signs people in and adds a signed identity header to every request, so the app never shows a login page or stores a password.
- Keeps people out who have not been given access to the app.
- Holds the roles your app declares, and lets an administrator give them to people.
- Creates a private database and passes its connection string in `DATABASE_URL` when `vmnodes.json` says `"database": true`.
- Passes a publish token and API address to the app when `vmnodes.json` lists something under `publishes`.
- Checks the new version answers before calling an update done, and keeps the old version running when an update fails.
- Scans the built image for serious security problems and refuses to put one online that has them.

## What your app must still do

- Listen on port 3000 on all addresses. VMnodes sets no `PORT` variable.
- Answer `GET /health` without asking anyone to sign in.
- Verify the identity header with `@vmnodes/identity`. Reading the token without checking its signature proves nothing.
- Check roles on the server, on every request that needs one.
- Read `DATABASE_URL` and keep anything worth keeping in that database.
- Declare roles, the database and shared record types in `vmnodes.json`.
- Send records to the publish API itself, if the app shares data.
- Escape any user text before putting it in a page.

## Related

- [Getting started](getting-started.md)
- [Sign-in and identity](concepts/sign-in-and-identity.md)
- [`vmnodes.json`](reference/vmnodes-json.md)
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md)

<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/getting-started.md -->

# Getting started

Take the VMnodes starter from nothing to a running app that you have tried, changed and updated. Read this first: every other page assumes you have done it once.

The starter is a team noticeboard. Anyone signed in can read notes, and people with the `starter.editor` role can post them. It already verifies sign-in, checks a role, keeps its notes in a database, shares them and answers `/health`.

## Before you start

You need three things:

1. **An org and an administrator account.** Sign-up is by invite today: ask your VMnodes contact for an invite code and the sign-up address. When sign-up finishes you are signed in at `https://apps.acme.vmnodes.com` (with your own org name in place of `acme`) as the org's administrator.
2. **Compute.** On the org's first screen, **Get your space ready**, press **Get compute**. The page counts through "Creating your host.", "Installing the software your apps run on." and "Setting up your web address.". It worked when the **Your apps** page offers **Put an app online**. Only an administrator sees this button.
3. **A git repository the platform can read**, and a computer with Node 22 or later, `npm` and `git`. The repository is either public at an `https://` address, or a private GitHub repository you give VMnodes access to in step 4.

## 1. Download the starter

```bash
curl -fsSLO https://docs.vmnodes.com/downloads/vmnodes-starter.tar.gz
tar -xzf vmnodes-starter.tar.gz
mv vmnodes-starter acme-notes
cd acme-notes
ls package.json vmnodes.json Dockerfile
```

It worked when `ls` prints all three names. The repository root must hold `package.json`, `vmnodes.json` and `Dockerfile`, because VMnodes reads them from the root.

## 2. Run it on your computer

```bash
npm install
npm test
npm run dev
```

`npm test` runs the app against a pretend sign-in gateway and ends with a line `passed=N failed=0`. If it does not, fix that before anything else.

`npm run dev` starts the app on port 3000 and a pretend portal on port 4100, and prints `Open http://127.0.0.1:4100 in your browser.` It keeps running until you press Ctrl+C. Open `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.

It worked when the page is headed **Noticeboard**, reads "Signed in as Eden Editor (editor@example.test)" and shows a **New note** box with a **Post note** button. The pretend portal signs you in as an editor.

Switch who you are by visiting these two addresses:

```
http://127.0.0.1:4100/_as/reader
http://127.0.0.1:4100/_as/editor
```

After `/_as/reader`, reload `http://127.0.0.1:4100`: the **New note** box is gone and the page reads "You can read notes. Posting needs the `starter.editor` role." After `/_as/editor` the box is back. Locally the page ends "Notes are kept in memory, so they are cleared when the app restarts or is updated." because `npm run dev` sets no database.

Stop the dev command with Ctrl+C.

## 3. Push it to a git repository

Create an empty repository on GitHub, then:

```bash
git init -b main
git add .
git commit -m "Start from the VMnodes starter"
git remote add origin https://github.com/acme/acme-notes.git
git push -u origin main
```

It worked when the repository's page on GitHub lists `server.js`, `vmnodes.json`, `Dockerfile` and `vendor`. VMnodes always builds the latest commit on the repository's default branch; you cannot choose another branch or a tag.

## 4. Put the app online

1. Sign in to your org's portal at `https://apps.acme.vmnodes.com`. The sign-in sends a six-digit code to your email. You land on **Your apps**.
2. Press **Put an app online**. The page of that name opens, with the section **1. Where is the code?**
   - **Public repository:** paste its `https://` address into **Or paste a public repository's URL**. The address must have no username, password or token in it.
   - **Private GitHub repository:** press **Connect GitHub**, install VMnodes Builds on that repository on GitHub's own screen, and you are brought back. Choose the repository from the **Repository** list. If it is not listed, open **Can't see your repo? Paste its URL**.
3. Under **2. Name it**, type `acme-notes` into **App name**. Use 3 to 30 lowercase letters, digits and hyphens, starting with a letter.
4. Press **Put it online**.

It worked when you land on a page headed `acme-notes` with a **Starting** badge. The **Build log** section shows the step it is on, one at a time: "Waiting to start…", "Creating your application…", "Building your image…", "Checking your image for security issues…" and "Deploying your app…". The page refreshes itself. A launch takes a few minutes.

## 5. Watch the launch

Leave the page open. The launch ends one of two ways.

- **It worked:** the badge reads **Working**. An **Open acme-notes** button and a **View app page** button appear. A line reads "You have every role acme-notes declares: starter.editor." The **Build log** ends "Your app is live."
- **It failed:** the badge reads **Not working**, a sentence says why, and a **Try again** button starts a new launch of the same name and repository. Look the sentence up in [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md).

If the page says "Your app is live, but your access to it couldn't be set up. Press Try again.", press **Try again** once: only the access step is retried.

## 6. Open the app

Press **Open acme-notes**. Your browser is already signed in, so the app opens at `https://acme-notes.acme.vmnodes.com`.

On a new app's first launch, the browser can show a certificate warning such as `ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID` for a few minutes after the badge reads **Working**, while the app's https certificate is issued. Wait a few minutes and reload. Never click through the warning.

It worked when the page is headed **Noticeboard**, reads "No notes yet.", shows a **New note** box, and ends "Notes are kept in this app's database, across restarts and updates." Type a note and press **Post note**: the page returns with your note in the list.

Two more addresses on the app show what the app sees. `/health` needs no identity from your app, so the platform's check can reach it. Opened in the browser you are signed in with, it shows, for example `{"status":"ok","app":"acme-notes","version":"0.1.0","buildCommit":"<40 characters>","publishing":true,"storage":"postgres"}`. `/api/me` lists who you are and your roles.

## 7. Take the role off yourself, then put it back

Seeing what a reader sees needs no second person.

1. On the launch page press **View app page**, then open the **People** tab.
2. Find the row marked "(you)". Its **Roles** column shows `starter.editor`. Press **Change roles**. A box opens headed "Change roles for" and your name.
3. Untick `starter.editor` and press **Save roles**. It worked when your row reads "No roles". Wait for that before you reload the app: a reload sent while the save is still finishing can show the old view. If it does, reload once more.
4. Reload the app. The **New note** box is gone and the page reads "You can read notes. Posting needs the `starter.editor` role. Ask whoever runs this app to give it to you." You can still open the app: taking a role away does not take away access.
5. Put the role back: **Change roles** on your row, tick `starter.editor`, **Save roles**. Reload the app. The **New note** box is back.

Nothing is redeployed. A role change reaches the app on your next request.

## 8. Change the app and update it

Change the heading, commit and push:

```bash
node -e 'const f="server.js",fs=require("fs");fs.writeFileSync(f,fs.readFileSync(f,"utf8").replace("<h1>Noticeboard</h1>","<h1>Team board</h1>"))'
npm test
git commit -am "Rename the heading"
git push
```

Then in the portal open the app's **People** tab and find the card headed **Deployment**. It shows "Current commit:" and the commit now running. Press **Update to latest commit**.

It worked when the card reads "Updating to" and the new commit, then "Your app is now running the latest commit." An update usually goes live within about two minutes. The card can keep reading "Updating to" for a while after the new version is live, so check the app itself: open `/health` in your signed-in browser. When its `buildCommit` is the commit you pushed, the update is live. Reload the app: the heading reads **Team board** and your notes are still there, because the starter's `vmnodes.json` says `"database": true`. If the update fails, the card reads "The update didn't go online, so your app is still running the previous version." and the old version keeps serving.

An update does not give you any role the new commit adds. Give yourself a new role with **Change roles**.

## What to read next

You have now done every step an app goes through. Your own app differs from the starter in its name, its roles and what it keeps. Pick the how-to that matches your task from the [index](index.md).

## Related

- [Sign-in and identity](concepts/sign-in-and-identity.md)
- [`vmnodes.json`](reference/vmnodes-json.md)
- [Apps](concepts/apps.md)
- [Troubleshooting](troubleshooting.md)

# Build a form-and-list app

Build an app where signed-in staff fill in a form and see every entry in a list, and only people you choose can use it. Read this when a customer asks for a sign-in book, a log, or any "add a row, see the rows" tool. The example is a visitor book for the org `acme`: reception signs visitors in and out, and the entries are kept in the app's database.

You start from the starter, so do [Getting started](../getting-started.md) steps 1 to 3 first. You then have a folder with `package.json`, `vmnodes.json`, `Dockerfile`, `server.js`, `store.js`, `publish.js` and `manifest.json`, and your own git repository.

## 1. Remove what this app does not use

This app shares nothing with other apps and does not use the advanced path, so delete both files that belong to them.

```bash
rm publish.js manifest.json
ls
```

It worked when `ls` lists `Dockerfile`, `package.json`, `server.js`, `store.js` and `vmnodes.json`, and does not list `publish.js` or `manifest.json`. Leaving `manifest.json` behind makes the launch page say your app mentions roles it does not declare, because it still names the starter's role.

## 2. Declare one role and a database

Replace `vmnodes.json` with this. The role is what reception needs to be given, and `"database": true` makes VMnodes create the app's database and pass its address in `DATABASE_URL`.

```json
{
  "apiVersion": "vmnodes.com/v1",
  "roles": [
    {
      "name": "visitors.staff",
      "description": "Can sign visitors in and out, and see who is on the visitor list."
    }
  ],
  "database": true
}
```

It worked when this prints `apiVersion roles database`:

```bash
node -e 'console.log(Object.keys(require("./vmnodes.json")).join(" "))'
```

The role name must be the same string in `vmnodes.json`, in `server.js` and in `dev/mock-portal.js`. [Roles](../concepts/roles.md) explains the format.

## 3. Replace `store.js`

`store.js` keeps the visits. One decision, made from `DATABASE_URL`, picks the database or memory, and the app refuses to start when the database is set but unreachable, instead of quietly keeping visits where the next restart loses them.

```js
// store.js: where the visits are kept.
//
// ONE decision, made here from DATABASE_URL:
//   DATABASE_URL set   visits are kept in Postgres, across restarts and updates.
//   not set            visits are kept in memory and cleared on every restart.
//
// On the platform, DATABASE_URL is set for you when vmnodes.json says
// "database": true. Locally it is not set, so `npm run dev` uses memory.
//
// There is no fallback. If DATABASE_URL is set but the database cannot be
// reached, the app refuses to start rather than quietly keeping visits in
// memory, where they would be lost at the next restart.

function memoryStore() {
  const visits = [];
  return {
    kind: "memory",
    async init() {},
    async list(limit = 100) { return visits.slice(0, limit).map((v) => ({ ...v })); },
    async add(visit) { visits.unshift({ ...visit, leftAt: null }); },
    // Returns the updated visit, or null when no visit with that id is still on site.
    async markLeft(id, leftAt) {
      const v = visits.find((x) => x.id === id && x.leftAt === null);
      if (!v) return null;
      v.leftAt = leftAt;
      return { ...v };
    },
    async close() {},
  };
}

function postgresStore(url, { attempts = 5, delayMs = 1000, log = console } = {}) {
  const postgres = require("postgres");
  const sql = postgres(url, { max: 3, onnotice: () => {} });
  const toVisit = (r) => ({
    id: r.id, visitor: r.visitor, company: r.company, visiting: r.visiting,
    arrivedAt: r.arrived_at.toISOString(), leftAt: r.left_at ? r.left_at.toISOString() : null,
  });
  return {
    kind: "postgres",
    async init() {
      for (let i = 1; ; i++) {
        try {
          await sql`create table if not exists visits (
            seq bigserial primary key,
            id uuid not null unique,
            visitor text not null,
            company text not null default '',
            visiting text not null,
            arrived_at timestamptz not null,
            left_at timestamptz
          )`;
          return;
        } catch (err) {
          if (i >= attempts) throw new Error(`could not reach the database after ${attempts} tries: ${err.message}`);
          log.log(`database not reachable yet (try ${i} of ${attempts}): ${err.message}`);
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, delayMs));
        }
      }
    },
    async list(limit = 100) {
      const rows = await sql`select id, visitor, company, visiting, arrived_at, left_at from visits order by seq desc limit ${limit}`;
      return rows.map(toVisit);
    },
    async add(v) {
      await sql`insert into visits (id, visitor, company, visiting, arrived_at)
                values (${v.id}, ${v.visitor}, ${v.company}, ${v.visiting}, ${v.arrivedAt})`;
    },
    async markLeft(id, leftAt) {
      const rows = await sql`update visits set left_at = ${leftAt} where id = ${id} and left_at is null
                             returning id, visitor, company, visiting, arrived_at, left_at`;
      return rows[0] ? toVisit(rows[0]) : null;
    },
    async close() { await sql.end({ timeout: 5 }); },
  };
}

function openStore({ env = process.env, log = console } = {}) {
  return env.DATABASE_URL ? postgresStore(env.DATABASE_URL, { log }) : memoryStore();
}

module.exports = { openStore };
```

## 4. Replace `server.js`

`server.js` is the whole app: the page with its form and list, the routes, and the checks that decide who may do what.

```js
// server.js: the whole app. A visitor book: people with the "staff" role sign
// visitors in when they arrive, see who has been in, and sign them out when they leave.
//
// APP_NAME is the name the app was put online as: the platform sets VMNODES_APP_NAME.
const http = require("node:http");
const crypto = require("node:crypto");
// Sign-in checking comes from the platform's own package, @vmnodes/identity.
const { VmnodesIdentity, IdentityError } = require("@vmnodes/identity");
const { openStore } = require("./store");

const APP_NAME = process.env.VMNODES_APP_NAME || "visitor-book";
// Must match the role name in vmnodes.json exactly ("visitors.staff").
const ROLE_PREFIX = "visitors";
const STAFF_ROLE = `${ROLE_PREFIX}.staff`;
const VERSION = require("./package.json").version;
// Set when the image is built (see Dockerfile). Reported as-is, never guessed.
const BUILD_COMMIT = process.env.BUILD_COMMIT || null;
// The platform does NOT set PORT: a portal launch sends traffic to port 3000, fixed.
// (PORT is only for local tests.)
const PORT = Number(process.env.PORT || 3000);
// Unset, the app listens on every address, which a container needs.
const LISTEN_ADDRESS = process.env.LISTEN_ADDRESS || undefined;

// Refuses to START if sign-in is not configured, so a misconfigured app never runs unprotected.
let identity;
try {
  identity = new VmnodesIdentity();
} catch (err) {
  console.error(`${err.message}\nThe platform sets these when your app is deployed; locally, \`npm run dev\` sets them for you.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const store = openStore();

const KEPT = {
  postgres: "Visits are kept in this app's database, across restarts and updates.",
  memory: "Visits are kept in memory, so they are cleared when the app restarts or is updated.",
};
const LIMITS = { visitor: 100, company: 100, visiting: 100 };
const UUID = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;

// Every piece of text a person typed goes through esc() before it goes into a page.
const esc = (s) => String(s).replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) => ({ "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;", "'": "&#39;" }[c]));

function send(res, status, body, type = "application/json") {
  res.writeHead(status, { "content-type": type });
  res.end(type === "application/json" ? JSON.stringify(body) : body);
}

function readBody(req, limit = 64 * 1024) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    let size = 0; const chunks = [];
    req.on("data", (c) => { size += c.length; if (size > limit) { reject(new IdentityError("body too large", 413)); req.destroy(); } else chunks.push(c); });
    req.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")));
    req.on("error", reject);
  });
}

// Reads the three fields from a form post or a JSON post. Trims, and never trusts the types.
async function readVisitFields(req) {
  const raw = await readBody(req);
  const get = (req.headers["content-type"] || "").includes("application/json")
    ? ((o) => (k) => (typeof o[k] === "string" ? o[k] : ""))(JSON.parse(raw || "{}"))
    : ((p) => (k) => p.get(k) || "")(new URLSearchParams(raw));
  return { visitor: get("visitor").trim(), company: get("company").trim(), visiting: get("visiting").trim() };
}

// The server-side checks. The form's `required` and `maxlength` are a courtesy to
// people; this is what actually decides, because anyone can send a request without the form.
function problemWith(f) {
  if (!f.visitor) return "visitor is required";
  if (!f.visiting) return "visiting is required";
  for (const k of Object.keys(LIMITS)) if (f[k].length > LIMITS[k]) return `${k} must be at most ${LIMITS[k]} characters`;
  return null;
}

const when = (iso) => iso.slice(0, 16).replace("T", " ");

function shell(title, inner) {
  return `<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>${esc(title)}</title>
<style>body{font:16px/1.5 system-ui,sans-serif;background:#0b0c10;color:#e8e8ee;max-width:760px;margin:0 auto;padding:16px}table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%}th,td{text-align:left;border-bottom:1px solid #2a2c35;padding:8px 6px}small,th{color:#9a9cab;font-weight:normal}label{display:block;margin-top:8px}input{width:100%;background:#15161c;color:inherit;border:1px solid #2a2c35;border-radius:6px;padding:8px;box-sizing:border-box;font:inherit}button{margin-top:8px;background:#5b5bd6;color:#fff;border:0;border-radius:6px;padding:10px 16px;font:inherit}.err{border:1px solid #d65b5b;border-radius:6px;padding:8px}code{font-family:ui-monospace,monospace}</style></head>
<body>${inner}</body></html>`;
}

function page(user, visits, { error = "", values = {} } = {}) {
  const rows = visits.length
    ? visits.map((v) => `<tr><td>${esc(v.visitor)}${v.company ? `<br><small>${esc(v.company)}</small>` : ""}</td><td>${esc(v.visiting)}</td><td>${esc(when(v.arrivedAt))}</td>
<td>${v.leftAt ? esc(when(v.leftAt)) : `<form method="post" action="/visits/${esc(v.id)}/leave"><button type="submit">Sign out</button></form>`}</td></tr>`).join("")
    : `<tr><td colspan="4">Nobody has signed in yet.</td></tr>`;
  const val = (k) => esc(values[k] || "");
  return shell("Visitor book", `<h1>Visitor book</h1><p id="who">Signed in as <strong>${esc(user.name || user.email)}</strong></p>
<form method="post" action="/visits">${error ? `<p class="err" role="alert">${esc(error)}</p>` : ""}
<label for="visitor">Visitor's name</label><input id="visitor" name="visitor" required maxlength="${LIMITS.visitor}" value="${val("visitor")}">
<label for="company">Company (optional)</label><input id="company" name="company" maxlength="${LIMITS.company}" value="${val("company")}">
<label for="visiting">Who are they here to see?</label><input id="visiting" name="visiting" required maxlength="${LIMITS.visiting}" value="${val("visiting")}">
<button type="submit">Sign in visitor</button></form>
<h2>Visitors</h2><table><thead><tr><th>Visitor</th><th>Visiting</th><th>Arrived</th><th>Left</th></tr></thead><tbody id="visits">${rows}</tbody></table>
<p id="kept"><small>${esc(KEPT[store.kind])}</small></p>`);
}

// A page on ANOTHER site can submit a form to this app, and the browser sends this app's
// sign-in with it. Every app on vmnodes.com counts as one "site", so the sign-in cookie's
// SameSite setting does not stop a page on another app. So refuse every write that the
// browser says came from anywhere but this app's own pages. A caller that is not a browser
// sends neither header and carries no sign-in cookie, so it is unaffected.
const CROSS_SITE_REFUSED = "a change sent from another site was refused";
function refuseCrossSiteWrite(req) {
  if (req.method === "GET" || req.method === "HEAD" || req.method === "OPTIONS") return;
  const site = req.headers["sec-fetch-site"];
  if (site) {
    if (site !== "same-origin" && site !== "none") throw new IdentityError(CROSS_SITE_REFUSED, 403);
    return;
  }
  const origin = req.headers.origin;
  if (origin && origin !== `https://${req.headers.host}`) throw new IdentityError(CROSS_SITE_REFUSED, 403);
}

async function handle(req, res) {
  const url = new URL(req.url, "http://app");
  const isApi = url.pathname.startsWith("/api/");

  // Health is checked by the platform directly, with no signed-in person, so
  // it must NOT require sign-in. It must also be honest: say what is running.
  if (url.pathname === "/health") {
    return send(res, 200, { status: "ok", app: APP_NAME, version: VERSION, buildCommit: BUILD_COMMIT, storage: store.kind });
  }

  // A change sent from another site is refused before anything else, whoever is signed in.
  refuseCrossSiteWrite(req);

  // Everything else: who is this? (Throws 401/503 if we cannot tell.)
  const user = await identity.currentUser(req.headers);
  // Every route below is for staff. Checked on the SERVER, on every request.
  identity.requireRole(user, STAFF_ROLE);

  if (url.pathname === "/" && req.method === "GET") return send(res, 200, page(user, await store.list()), "text/html; charset=utf-8");
  if (url.pathname === "/api/visits" && req.method === "GET") return send(res, 200, { items: await store.list() });

  if ((url.pathname === "/visits" || url.pathname === "/api/visits") && req.method === "POST") {
    const fields = await readVisitFields(req);
    const problem = problemWith(fields);
    if (problem) {
      if (isApi) return send(res, 400, { error: problem });
      return send(res, 400, page(user, await store.list(), { error: problem, values: fields }), "text/html; charset=utf-8");
    }
    const visit = { id: crypto.randomUUID(), ...fields, arrivedAt: new Date().toISOString() };
    await store.add(visit);
    if (!isApi) { res.writeHead(303, { location: "/" }); return res.end(); }
    return send(res, 201, { ...visit, leftAt: null });
  }

  const leave = url.pathname.match(/^\/(?:api\/)?visits\/([^/]+)\/leave$/);
  if (leave && req.method === "POST") {
    // An id that is not a UUID can never match a row; say so here instead of letting the database throw.
    const visit = UUID.test(leave[1]) ? await store.markLeft(leave[1].toLowerCase(), new Date().toISOString()) : null;
    if (!visit) return send(res, 404, { error: "no such visitor on site" });
    if (!isApi) { res.writeHead(303, { location: "/" }); return res.end(); }
    return send(res, 200, visit);
  }

  return send(res, 404, { error: "not found" });
}

const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
  handle(req, res).catch((err) => {
    const status = err instanceof IdentityError ? err.status : err instanceof SyntaxError ? 400 : 500;
    if (status >= 500) console.error(err.cause || err);
    const message = status === 500 ? "something went wrong" : err.message;
    if (new URL(req.url, "http://app").pathname.startsWith("/api/")) return send(res, status, { error: message });
    send(res, status, shell("Visitor book", `<h1>Visitor book</h1><p>${esc(message)}</p>${status === 403 ? (message === CROSS_SITE_REFUSED ? "<p>Nothing was changed. To make this change, open this app and use its own page.</p>" : `<p>This app is for people with the <code>${esc(STAFF_ROLE)}</code> role. Ask whoever runs it to give it to you.</p>`) : ""}`), "text/html; charset=utf-8");
  });
});
store.init().then(
  () => server.listen({ port: PORT, host: LISTEN_ADDRESS }, () => console.log(`${APP_NAME} ${VERSION} listening on :${server.address().port} (visits kept in ${store.kind})`)),
  (err) => {
    // No fallback to memory: visits kept there would be lost at the next restart.
    console.error(`${err.message}\nDATABASE_URL is set, so this app will not start without its database.`);
    process.exit(1);
  },
);
```

It worked when both files parse. This prints nothing and exits 0:

```bash
node --check server.js && node --check store.js
```

## 6. Replace the test

The starter's `npm test` checks the noticeboard, so it fails once `server.js` changes. Replace `test/smoke.js` with this. Every refused case has an accepted case beside it, so a check that can only ever refuse cannot pass by accident, and the run ends with a count.

```js
// test/smoke.js: `npm test`. Proves the visitor book refuses what it should and
// accepts what it should. Every "refused" row has a matching "accepted" row, so a
// check that can only ever refuse cannot pass by accident.
const { spawn } = require("node:child_process");
const http = require("node:http");
const path = require("node:path");
const { SignJWT } = require("jose");
const { startMockPortal } = require("../dev/mock-portal");

const APP_ID = "app_smoke_test";
const SERVER = path.join(__dirname, "..", "server.js");
const children = [];
let pass = 0, fail = 0;
function check(name, got, want) {
  const ok = JSON.stringify(got) === JSON.stringify(want);
  ok ? pass++ : fail++;
  console.log(`${ok ? "ok  " : "FAIL"} ${name}${ok ? "" : `  (expected ${JSON.stringify(want)}, got ${JSON.stringify(got)})`}`);
}

function startApp(env) {
  return new Promise((resolve) => {
    const child = spawn(process.execPath, [SERVER], { env: { PATH: process.env.PATH, PORT: "0", LISTEN_ADDRESS: "127.0.0.1", ...env }, stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "pipe"] });
    children.push(child);
    let out = "";
    const onData = (d) => {
      out += d;
      const m = out.match(/listening on :(\d+)/);
      if (m) resolve({ child, url: `http://127.0.0.1:${m[1]}`, out: () => out });
    };
    child.stdout.on("data", onData); child.stderr.on("data", onData);
    child.on("exit", (code) => resolve({ child, exited: code, out: () => out }));
  });
}

function request(url, { method = "GET", headers = {}, body } = {}) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    const req = http.request(url, { method, headers }, (res) => {
      let data = ""; res.on("data", (d) => (data += d));
      res.on("end", () => resolve({ status: res.statusCode, headers: res.headers, body: data, json: () => JSON.parse(data) }));
    });
    req.on("error", reject);
    if (body) req.write(body);
    req.end();
  });
}

(async () => {
  // --- 1. It refuses to start without sign-in configured -------------------
  const noAppId = await startApp({ VMNODES_PORTAL_URL: "http://127.0.0.1:1" });
  check("refuses to START without VMNODES_APP_ID", noAppId.exited !== undefined && noAppId.exited !== 0, true);

  const portal = await startMockPortal({ port: 0, appId: APP_ID });
  const app = await startApp({ VMNODES_PORTAL_URL: portal.issuer, VMNODES_APP_ID: APP_ID });
  check("CONTROL: starts when both settings are present", typeof app.url, "string");
  if (!app.url) { console.log(app.out()); process.exit(1); }
  portal.setTarget(app.url);

  const mint = (claims, { aud = APP_ID } = {}) =>
    new SignJWT({ email: "e@example.test", name: "Eden Editor", kind: "employee", groups: [], roles: [], ...claims })
      .setProtectedHeader({ alg: "RS256", kid: "local-dev" }).setSubject("usr_1").setIssuer(portal.issuer).setAudience(aud)
      .setIssuedAt().setExpirationTime("5m").sign(portal.privateKey);
  const as = async (claims, opts) => ({ "x-vmnodes-identity": await mint(claims, opts) });
  const staff = () => as({ roles: ["visitors.staff"] });
  const nobody = () => as({ name: "Riley Reader", roles: [] });
  const json = (headers, method, p, body) => request(`${app.url}${p}`, { method, headers: { ...headers, "content-type": "application/json" }, body: body === undefined ? undefined : JSON.stringify(body) });

  // --- 2. Health and sign-in -------------------------------------------------
  const h = await request(`${app.url}/health`);
  check("health answers 200 WITHOUT sign-in", h.status, 200);
  check("health says visits are kept in memory when DATABASE_URL is not set", h.json().storage, "memory");
  check("CONTROL: a staff token is accepted", (await json(await staff(), "GET", "/api/visits")).status, 200);
  check("no identity header -> 401", (await request(`${app.url}/api/visits`)).status, 401);
  check("token meant for ANOTHER app -> 401", (await json(await as({ roles: ["visitors.staff"] }, { aud: "app_someone_else" }), "GET", "/api/visits")).status, 401);

  // --- 3. The role is checked on the server, for every route -----------------
  check("signed in without the role: list -> 403", (await json(await nobody(), "GET", "/api/visits")).status, 403);
  check("signed in without the role: sign in a visitor -> 403", (await json(await nobody(), "POST", "/api/visits", { visitor: "A", visiting: "B" })).status, 403);
  check("signed in without the role: sign out -> 403", (await json(await nobody(), "POST", "/api/visits/6f1c2a52-8f0d-4d64-9d0e-1c7b0e2a9b11/leave")).status, 403);

  // --- 4. Adding and listing -------------------------------------------------
  const made = await json(await staff(), "POST", "/api/visits", { visitor: "Ada <b>Lovelace</b>", company: "Analytical Ltd", visiting: "Grace" });
  check("CONTROL: a valid visit is accepted -> 201", made.status, 201);
  const list = (await json(await staff(), "GET", "/api/visits")).json().items;
  check("the visit is in the list, with no left time", [list.length, list[0].visitor, list[0].leftAt], [1, "Ada <b>Lovelace</b>", null]);
  for (const [name, body] of [["no visitor", { visiting: "Grace" }], ["blank visitor", { visitor: "   ", visiting: "Grace" }], ["no visiting", { visitor: "Ada" }], ["a number for visitor", { visitor: 5, visiting: "Grace" }], ["a 101-character visitor", { visitor: "x".repeat(101), visiting: "Grace" }]]) {
    check(`${name} -> 400`, (await json(await staff(), "POST", "/api/visits", body)).status, 400);
  }
  const broken = await request(`${app.url}/api/visits`, { method: "POST", headers: { ...(await staff()), "content-type": "application/json" }, body: "{nope" });
  check("a body that is not JSON -> 400", broken.status, 400);
  check("nothing was added by the refused posts", (await json(await staff(), "GET", "/api/visits")).json().items.length, 1);

  // --- 5. Text is escaped when it goes into the page -------------------------
  portal.setUser("editor");
  const pageHtml = (await request(`${portal.issuer}/`)).body;
  check("typed text is escaped, not run as markup", pageHtml.includes("Ada &lt;b&gt;Lovelace&lt;/b&gt;") && !pageHtml.includes("<b>Lovelace"), true);
  portal.setUser("reader");
  check("a person without the role gets a 403 page, not the list", [(await request(`${portal.issuer}/`)).status, (await request(`${portal.issuer}/`)).body.includes("Lovelace")], [403, false]);
  portal.setUser("editor");

  // --- 6. Signing out --------------------------------------------------------
  const id = made.json().id;
  const out = await json(await staff(), "POST", `/api/visits/${id}/leave`);
  check("CONTROL: signing out a visitor on site -> 200, with a left time", [out.status, typeof out.json().leftAt], [200, "string"]);
  check("signing out the same visitor again -> 404", (await json(await staff(), "POST", `/api/visits/${id}/leave`)).status, 404);
  check("a made-up id -> 404", (await json(await staff(), "POST", "/api/visits/6f1c2a52-8f0d-4d64-9d0e-1c7b0e2a9b11/leave")).status, 404);
  check("an id that is not a UUID -> 404, not a database error", (await json(await staff(), "POST", "/api/visits/not-an-id/leave")).status, 404);

  // --- 7. Changes sent from another site are refused, whoever is signed in ----
  // A form on another app's page must not add a visitor as the signed-in person.
  const formPost = async (extra) => request(`${app.url}/visits`, { method: "POST", headers: { ...(await staff()), "content-type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", ...extra }, body: "visitor=From+elsewhere&visiting=Grace" });
  const viaBrowser = async (extra) => (await formPost(extra)).status;
  check("a form post from ANOTHER site -> 403", await viaBrowser({ "sec-fetch-site": "cross-site" }), 403);
  const refusal = (await formPost({ "sec-fetch-site": "cross-site" })).body;
  check("the refusal page says nothing was changed, and does not say a role is missing", [refusal.includes("Nothing was changed"), refusal.includes("Ask whoever runs it")], [true, false]);
  check("a form post from a SIBLING app on the same site -> 403", await viaBrowser({ "sec-fetch-site": "same-site" }), 403);
  check("a post with a foreign Origin and no fetch metadata -> 403", await viaBrowser({ origin: "https://evil.example" }), 403);
  const crossSiteVisits = (await json(await staff(), "GET", "/api/visits")).json().items.filter((v) => v.visitor === "From elsewhere").length;
  check("...and none of those three posts was saved", crossSiteVisits, 0);
  check("CONTROL: the app's own form (same-origin) still posts -> 303", await viaBrowser({ "sec-fetch-site": "same-origin" }), 303);

  // --- 8. A database that cannot be reached stops the app; it never falls back --
  const noDb = await startApp({ VMNODES_PORTAL_URL: portal.issuer, VMNODES_APP_ID: APP_ID, DATABASE_URL: "postgres://visitors@127.0.0.1:1/visitors" });
  check("with DATABASE_URL set and no database, the app refuses to START", noDb.exited !== undefined && noDb.exited !== 0, true);
  check("...and says it will not start without its database", /will not start without its database/.test(noDb.out()), true);

  // --- 9. The count itself: zero checks run must never read as a pass ---------
  const FLOOR = 31;
  if (pass + fail < FLOOR) { console.log(`FAIL only ${pass + fail} checks ran, expected at least ${FLOOR}`); fail++; }
  console.log(`\npassed=${pass} failed=${fail}`);
  finish(fail === 0 ? 0 : 1);
})().catch((e) => { console.error("smoke test crashed:", e); finish(1); });

function finish(code) {
  for (const c of children) if (c.exitCode === null) c.kill();
  process.exit(code);
}
```

```bash
npm test
```

It worked when the last line is `passed=33 failed=0`. A run that ends without a `passed=` line is broken plumbing, not a broken app: read the first line that starts `FAIL` or the error above it.


It prints `Open http://127.0.0.1:4100 in your browser.` Open that address.

It worked when the page is headed **Visitor book**, reads "Signed in as Eden Editor", shows a form with **Visitor's name**, **Company (optional)** and **Who are they here to see?**, and a **Sign in visitor** button, and the table says "Nobody has signed in yet." Fill the form in and press **Sign in visitor**: the visitor appears in the table with a **Sign out** button, and pressing it fills the **Left** column. The last line reads "Visits are kept in memory, so they are cleared when the app restarts or is updated." because `npm run dev` sets no database.

Now see what a person without the role sees. Open `http://127.0.0.1:4100/_as/reader`. ## Check it works

Run these in order. Items 2 to 5 need `npm run dev` running in another terminal, started as the default user `editor`.

1. `npm test` ends `passed=33 failed=0`.
2. Adding through the form answers `303`, and the entry is in the list:

   ```bash
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' -X POST -d 'visitor=Ada&company=Analytical&visiting=Grace' http://127.0.0.1:4100/visits
   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4100/api/visits
   ```

   The first prints `303`. The second prints one item with `"visitor":"Ada"` and `"leftAt":null`.
3. The server refuses an empty name even when the form is bypassed. This prints `{"error":"visitor is required"}`:

   ```bash
   curl -s -X POST -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"visitor":"","visiting":"Grace"}' http://127.0.0.1:4100/api/visits
   ```
4. A request with no identity header is refused. Port 3000 is the app itself, with no portal in front. This prints `401`:

   ```bash
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:3000/api/visits
   ```
5. A signed-in person without the role is refused, and signing back in lets them through:

   ```bash
   curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:4100/_as/reader
   curl -s http://127.0.0.1:4100/api/visits
   curl -s -o /dev/null http://127.0.0.1:4100/_as/editor
   curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' http://127.0.0.1:4100/api/visits
   ```

   The second command prints `{"error":"role 'visitors.staff' required"}`. The last prints `200`.
6. After the launch, open `https://visitor-book.acme.vmnodes.com/health` in the browser you are signed in with. It says where visits are kept: it shows `"status":"ok"` and `"storage":"postgres"`. `"storage":"memory"` means `"database": true` did not reach the deployed commit.

## Traps

- **Dates shown in UTC.** The visitor book stores and shows UTC times to stay short. If your list shows dates, decides what is overdue or defaults to "today", follow [Dates and time zones](dates-and-time-zones.md) instead.

- **Hiding the form is not checking the role.** Call `identity.requireRole` on the server for every route that reads or writes, as `server.js` does. A person without the role who sends a request directly gets through otherwise. Check 5 tests it.
- **The role string must match in three places**: `vmnodes.json`, `server.js` and `dev/mock-portal.js`. A role the code checks but `vmnodes.json` does not declare can never be given to anyone.
- **An update does not give anyone a role the new commit adds.** If you add a role later, give it with **Change roles**. See [Roles](../concepts/roles.md).
- **Validate on the server.** The form's `required` and `maxlength` are courtesy for people; anyone can send a request without the form. Check 3 tests it.
- **Escape every typed value before it goes into a page.** `server.js` passes each one through `esc()`. Without it a visitor named `<b>Ada</b>` is run as markup.
- **A fixed id in a URL can be anything.** The leave route checks the id is a UUID before it reaches the database, so a made-up id answers 404 and not a database error.
- **Do not fall back to memory.** With `DATABASE_URL` set, an unreachable database must stop the app. A silent fallback loses every entry at the next restart. Without `"database": true`, an update clears the data too. See [Data](../concepts/data.md).
- **List every file the server loads in the `Dockerfile`'s `COPY` line.** A file you add and forget builds, then fails with "Your app stopped while starting." A file you delete and leave in the list fails the build.
- **Keep the app answering `/health` with no sign-in, and keep it on port 3000.** The starter does both. See [Apps](../concepts/apps.md).

<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/how-to/approvals.md -->

# Submit and approve

Build an app where one person raises a request and a different person approves or rejects it, with the rule enforced by the server and not by what the page shows. Read this for purchase, expense, leave or any other sign-off. The example is purchase requests at the org `acme`, approved by the budget holder.

You start from the starter, so do [Getting started](../getting-started.md) steps 1 to 3 first. This page assumes the file layout and the pretend portal explained in [Build a form-and-list app](form-and-list.md); only what differs is repeated here.

## Who may do what

| Role | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| `purchasing.requester` | raise a request; see only the requests they raised | see anyone else's; approve or reject |
| `purchasing.approver` | see every request; approve or reject one, with an optional reason | decide a request they raised themselves |
| neither | nothing: the app answers 403 | |

A person can hold both roles. They can then raise and see everything, but still cannot decide their own request.

## 1. Remove what this app does not use

```bash
rm publish.js manifest.json test/smoke.js
ls
```

It worked when `ls` lists `Dockerfile`, `package.json`, `server.js`, `store.js` and `vmnodes.json`, and does not list `publish.js` or `manifest.json`.

## 2. Declare both roles and a database

Replace `vmnodes.json`. Each role's `description` is what an administrator reads before giving it, so it says what the person can then do.

```json
{
  "apiVersion": "vmnodes.com/v1",
  "roles": [
    {
      "name": "purchasing.requester",
      "description": "Can raise purchase requests and see the ones they raised."
    },
    {
      "name": "purchasing.approver",
      "description": "Can see every purchase request and approve or reject them."
    }
  ],
  "database": true
}
```

It worked when this prints `purchasing.requester purchasing.approver`:

```bash
node -e 'console.log(require("./vmnodes.json").roles.map((r) => r.name).join(" "))'
```

## 3. Replace `store.js`

The request's owner is kept as `owner_id`, which is the identity's `id`. An `id` never changes for a person, and an email address can be reused or changed, so never key on the email. The `where status = 'pending'` in `decide` is what stops two approvers deciding the same request.

```js
// store.js: where the purchase requests are kept.
//
//   DATABASE_URL set   requests are kept in Postgres, across restarts and updates.
//   not set            requests are kept in memory and cleared on every restart.
//
// On the platform, DATABASE_URL is set for you when vmnodes.json says
// "database": true. There is no fallback: if DATABASE_URL is set but the
// database cannot be reached, the app refuses to start.
//
// A request's owner is kept as owner_id: the identity's `id`, which never changes
// for a person. Never key on email: an address can be reused or changed.

function memoryStore() {
  const rows = [];
  return {
    kind: "memory",
    async init() {},
    // ownerId: only that person's requests; null: everyone's (for approvers).
    async list(ownerId) { return rows.filter((r) => ownerId === null || r.ownerId === ownerId).map((r) => ({ ...r })); },
    async get(id) { const r = rows.find((x) => x.id === id); return r ? { ...r } : null; },
    async add(r) { rows.unshift({ ...r, status: "pending", decidedById: null, decidedByName: null, decidedAt: null, note: "" }); },
    // Only a pending request can be decided. Returns the request, or null if it was not pending.
    async decide(id, { status, byId, byName, note, at }) {
      const r = rows.find((x) => x.id === id && x.status === "pending");
      if (!r) return null;
      Object.assign(r, { status, decidedById: byId, decidedByName: byName, note, decidedAt: at });
      return { ...r };
    },
    async close() {},
  };
}

function postgresStore(url, { attempts = 5, delayMs = 1000, log = console } = {}) {
  const postgres = require("postgres");
  const sql = postgres(url, { max: 3, onnotice: () => {} });
  const cols = sql`id, owner_id, owner_name, item, amount_cents, created_at, status, decided_by_id, decided_by_name, decided_at, note`;
  const toRequest = (r) => ({
    id: r.id, ownerId: r.owner_id, ownerName: r.owner_name, item: r.item, amountCents: r.amount_cents,
    createdAt: r.created_at.toISOString(), status: r.status, decidedById: r.decided_by_id, decidedByName: r.decided_by_name,
    decidedAt: r.decided_at ? r.decided_at.toISOString() : null, note: r.note,
  });
  return {
    kind: "postgres",
    async init() {
      for (let i = 1; ; i++) {
        try {
          await sql`create table if not exists requests (
            seq bigserial primary key,
            id uuid not null unique,
            owner_id text not null,
            owner_name text not null,
            item text not null,
            amount_cents integer not null,
            created_at timestamptz not null,
            status text not null default 'pending' check (status in ('pending', 'approved', 'rejected')),
            decided_by_id text,
            decided_by_name text,
            decided_at timestamptz,
            note text not null default ''
          )`;
          await sql`create index if not exists requests_owner_idx on requests (owner_id)`;
          return;
        } catch (err) {
          if (i >= attempts) throw new Error(`could not reach the database after ${attempts} tries: ${err.message}`);
          log.log(`database not reachable yet (try ${i} of ${attempts}): ${err.message}`);
          await new Promise((r) => setTimeout(r, delayMs));
        }
      }
    },
    async list(ownerId) {
      const rows = ownerId === null
        ? await sql`select ${cols} from requests order by seq desc`
        : await sql`select ${cols} from requests where owner_id = ${ownerId} order by seq desc`;
      return rows.map(toRequest);
    },
    async get(id) {
      const rows = await sql`select ${cols} from requests where id = ${id}`;
      return rows[0] ? toRequest(rows[0]) : null;
    },
    async add(r) {
      await sql`insert into requests (id, owner_id, owner_name, item, amount_cents, created_at)
                values (${r.id}, ${r.ownerId}, ${r.ownerName}, ${r.item}, ${r.amountCents}, ${r.createdAt})`;
    },
    // The "where status = 'pending'" is what stops two approvers deciding the same request.
    async decide(id, { status, byId, byName, note, at }) {
      const rows = await sql`update requests set status = ${status}, decided_by_id = ${byId}, decided_by_name = ${byName}, note = ${note}, decided_at = ${at}
                             where id = ${id} and status = 'pending' returning ${cols}`;
      return rows[0] ? toRequest(rows[0]) : null;
    },
    async close() { await sql.end({ timeout: 5 }); },
  };
}

function openStore({ env = process.env, log = console } = {}) {
  return env.DATABASE_URL ? postgresStore(env.DATABASE_URL, { log }) : memoryStore();
}

module.exports = { openStore };
```

## 4. Replace `server.js`

The checks that matter are in the routes: scope for reading, `requireRole` for deciding, the own-request rule, and the same 404 for a request that is missing and one that is not yours.

```js
// server.js: the whole app. Purchase requests: people with the "requester" role raise
// a request, and people with the "approver" role approve or reject it.
//
// Who may do what, and every one of these is checked on the SERVER:
//   requester   raise a request; see only the requests they raised
//   approver    see every request; approve or reject one (never their own)
const http = require("node:http");
const crypto = require("node:crypto");
const { VmnodesIdentity, IdentityError } = require("@vmnodes/identity");
const { openStore } = require("./store");

const APP_NAME = process.env.VMNODES_APP_NAME || "purchase-requests";
// Must match the role names in vmnodes.json exactly.
const ROLE_PREFIX = "purchasing";
const REQUESTER_ROLE = `${ROLE_PREFIX}.requester`;
const APPROVER_ROLE = `${ROLE_PREFIX}.approver`;
const VERSION = require("./package.json").version;
const BUILD_COMMIT = process.env.BUILD_COMMIT || null;
const PORT = Number(process.env.PORT || 3000);
const LISTEN_ADDRESS = process.env.LISTEN_ADDRESS || undefined;

let identity;
try {
  identity = new VmnodesIdentity();
} catch (err) {
  console.error(`${err.message}\nThe platform sets these when your app is deployed; locally, \`npm run dev\` sets them for you.`);
  process.exit(1);
}
const store = openStore();

const UUID = /^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$/i;
const money = (cents) => (cents / 100).toFixed(2);
const esc = (s) => String(s).replace(/[&<>"']/g, (c) => ({ "&": "&amp;", "<": "&lt;", ">": "&gt;", '"': "&quot;", "'": "&#39;" }[c]));

function send(res, status, body, type = "application/json") {
  res.writeHead(status, { "content-type": type });
  res.end(type === "application/json" ? JSON.stringify(body) : body);
}

function readBody(req, limit = 64 * 1024) {
  return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
    let size = 0; const chunks = [];
    req.on("data", (c) => { size += c.length; if (size > limit) { reject(new IdentityError("body too large", 413)); req.destroy(); } else chunks.push(c); });
    req.on("end", () => resolve(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8")));
    req.on("error", reject);
  });
}

// Reads named text fields from a form post or a JSON post. Never trusts the types.
async function readFields(req, names) {
  const raw = await readBody(req);
  const json = (req.headers["content-type"] || "").includes("application/json");
  const o = json ? JSON.parse(raw || "{}") : Object.fromEntries(new URLSearchParams(raw));
  return Object.fromEntries(names.map((n) => [n, typeof o[n] === "string" || typeof o[n] === "number" ? String(o[n]).trim() : ""]));
}

// "12", "12.5" and "12.50" are fine; "-3", "1e3" and "12.345" are not. Returns whole cents, or null.
function parseAmount(text) {
  const m = /^(\d{1,7})(?:\.(\d{1,2}))?$/.exec(text);
  if (!m) return null;
  const cents = Number(m[1]) * 100 + Number((m[2] || "").padEnd(2, "0"));
  return cents > 0 ? cents : null;
}

const holds = (user, role) => user.roles.includes(role);

function view(r) {
  return { id: r.id, ownerName: r.ownerName, item: r.item, amount: money(r.amountCents), createdAt: r.createdAt, status: r.status, decidedByName: r.decidedByName, decidedAt: r.decidedAt, note: r.note };
}

function shell(inner) {
  return `<!doctype html><html lang="en"><head><meta charset="utf-8"><meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1"><title>Purchase requests</title>
<style>body{font:16px/1.5 system-ui,sans-serif;background:#0b0c10;color:#e8e8ee;max-width:820px;margin:0 auto;padding:16px}table{border-collapse:collapse;width:100%}th,td{text-align:left;border-bottom:1px solid #2a2c35;padding:8px 6px;vertical-align:top}small,th{color:#9a9cab;font-weight:normal}label{display:block;margin-top:8px}input{width:100%;background:#15161c;color:inherit;border:1px solid #2a2c35;border-radius:6px;padding:8px;box-sizing:border-box;font:inherit}button{margin:8px 8px 0 0;background:#5b5bd6;color:#fff;border:0;border-radius:6px;padding:8px 14px;font:inherit}.err{border:1px solid #d65b5b;border-radius:6px;padding:8px}code{font-family:ui-monospace,monospace}</style></head><body>${inner}</body></html>`;
}

function page(user, requests, { error = "", values = {} } = {}) {
  const approver = holds(user, APPROVER_ROLE);
  const rows = requests.length
    ? requests.map((r) => {
      // Showing the buttons only to approvers is a courtesy. The server checks the role again on every decision.
      const decide = r.status === "pending" && approver && r.ownerId !== user.id
        ? `<form method="post" action="/requests/${esc(r.id)}/decision"><input name="note" maxlength="300" placeholder="Reason (optional)" aria-label="Reason"><button name="decision" value="approve" type="submit">Approve</button><button name="decision" value="reject" type="submit">Reject</button></form>`
        : "";
      const outcome = r.status === "pending" ? "Waiting" : `${esc(r.status === "approved" ? "Approved" : "Rejected")} by ${esc(r.decidedByName)}${r.note ? `<br><small>${esc(r.note)}</small>` : ""}`;
      return `<tr><td>${esc(r.item)}<br><small>${esc(r.ownerName)}</small></td><td>${esc(money(r.amountCents))}</td><td>${outcome}${decide}</td></tr>`;
    }).join("")
    : `<tr><td colspan="3">No requests yet.</td></tr>`;
  const form = holds(user, REQUESTER_ROLE)
    ? `<form method="post" action="/requests">${error ? `<p class="err" role="alert">${esc(error)}</p>` : ""}
<label for="item">What do you need?</label><input id="item" name="item" required maxlength="200" value="${esc(values.item || "")}">
<label for="amount">Cost</label><input id="amount" name="amount" required inputmode="decimal" placeholder="49.90" value="${esc(values.amount || "")}">
<button type="submit">Send request</button></form>`
    : `<p>You can see and decide requests. Raising one needs the <code>${esc(REQUESTER_ROLE)}</code> role.</p>`;
  return shell(`<h1>Purchase requests</h1><p id="who">Signed in as <strong>${esc(user.name || user.email)}</strong>${approver ? " (approver)" : ""}</p>${form}
<h2>${approver ? "All requests" : "Your requests"}</h2><table><thead><tr><th>Request</th><th>Cost</th><th>Status</th></tr></thead><tbody id="requests">${rows}</tbody></table>`);
}

// A page on ANOTHER site can submit a form to this app, and the browser sends this app's
// sign-in with it. Every app on vmnodes.com counts as one "site", so the sign-in cookie's
// SameSite setting does not stop a page on another app. So refuse every write that the
// browser says came from anywhere but this app's own pages. A caller that is not a browser
// sends neither header and carries no sign-in cookie, so it is unaffected.
const CROSS_SITE_REFUSED = "a change sent from another site was refused";
function refuseCrossSiteWrite(req) {
  if (req.method === "GET" || req.method === "HEAD" || req.method === "OPTIONS") return;
  const site = req.headers["sec-fetch-site"];
  if (site) {
    if (site !== "same-origin" && site !== "none") throw new IdentityError(CROSS_SITE_REFUSED, 403);
    return;
  }
  const origin = req.headers.origin;
  if (origin && origin !== `https://${req.headers.host}`) throw new IdentityError(CROSS_SITE_REFUSED, 403);
}

async function handle(req, res) {
  const url = new URL(req.url, "http://app");
  const isApi = url.pathname.startsWith("/api/");

  if (url.pathname === "/health") {
    return send(res, 200, { status: "ok", app: APP_NAME, version: VERSION, buildCommit: BUILD_COMMIT, storage: store.kind });
  }

  // A change sent from another site is refused before anything else, whoever is signed in.
  refuseCrossSiteWrite(req);

  const user = await identity.currentUser(req.headers);
  // Holding neither role means no business here at all.
  if (!holds(user, REQUESTER_ROLE) && !holds(user, APPROVER_ROLE)) {
    throw new IdentityError(`role '${REQUESTER_ROLE}' or '${APPROVER_ROLE}' required`, 403);
  }
  // Approvers see everything; everyone else sees only what they raised. The key is user.id, never the email.
  const scope = () => (holds(user, APPROVER_ROLE) ? null : user.id);

  if (url.pathname === "/" && req.method === "GET") return send(res, 200, page(user, await store.list(scope())), "text/html; charset=utf-8");
  if (url.pathname === "/api/requests" && req.method === "GET") return send(res, 200, { items: (await store.list(scope())).map(view) });

  const one = url.pathname.match(/^\/api\/requests\/([^/]+)$/);
  if (one && req.method === "GET") {
    const r = UUID.test(one[1]) ? await store.get(one[1].toLowerCase()) : null;
    // Someone else's request and a request that does not exist get the SAME answer, so nobody can probe for ids.
    if (!r || (scope() !== null && r.ownerId !== user.id)) return send(res, 404, { error: "no such request" });
    return send(res, 200, view(r));
  }

  if ((url.pathname === "/requests" || url.pathname === "/api/requests") && req.method === "POST") {
    identity.requireRole(user, REQUESTER_ROLE);
    const f = await readFields(req, ["item", "amount"]);
    const amountCents = parseAmount(f.amount);
    const problem = !f.item ? "item is required" : f.item.length > 200 ? "item must be at most 200 characters"
      : amountCents === null ? "amount must be a positive number with at most two decimals" : null;
    if (problem) {
      if (isApi) return send(res, 400, { error: problem });
      return send(res, 400, page(user, await store.list(scope()), { error: problem, values: f }), "text/html; charset=utf-8");
    }
    const r = { id: crypto.randomUUID(), ownerId: user.id, ownerName: user.name || user.email, item: f.item, amountCents, createdAt: new Date().toISOString() };
    await store.add(r);
    if (!isApi) { res.writeHead(303, { location: "/" }); return res.end(); }
    return send(res, 201, view({ ...r, status: "pending", decidedByName: null, decidedAt: null, note: "" }));
  }

  const decision = url.pathname.match(/^\/(?:api\/)?requests\/([^/]+)\/decision$/);
  if (decision && req.method === "POST") {
    identity.requireRole(user, APPROVER_ROLE); // checked on the SERVER, whatever the page showed
    const f = await readFields(req, ["decision", "note"]);
    if (f.decision !== "approve" && f.decision !== "reject") return send(res, 400, { error: "decision must be approve or reject" });
    if (f.note.length > 300) return send(res, 400, { error: "note must be at most 300 characters" });
    const r = UUID.test(decision[1]) ? await store.get(decision[1].toLowerCase()) : null;
    if (!r) return send(res, 404, { error: "no such request" });
    if (r.ownerId === user.id) return send(res, 403, { error: "you cannot decide your own request" });
    const decided = await store.decide(r.id, { status: f.decision === "approve" ? "approved" : "rejected", byId: user.id, byName: user.name || user.email, note: f.note, at: new Date().toISOString() });
    if (!decided) return send(res, 409, { error: "this request has already been decided" });
    if (!isApi) { res.writeHead(303, { location: "/" }); return res.end(); }
    return send(res, 200, view(decided));
  }

  return send(res, 404, { error: "not found" });
}

const server = http.createServer((req, res) => {
  handle(req, res).catch((err) => {
    const status = err instanceof IdentityError ? err.status : err instanceof SyntaxError ? 400 : 500;
    if (status >= 500) console.error(err.cause || err);
    const message = status === 500 ? "something went wrong" : err.message;
    if (new URL(req.url, "http://app").pathname.startsWith("/api/")) return send(res, status, { error: message });
    send(res, status, shell(`<h1>Purchase requests</h1><p>${esc(message)}</p>${status === 403 ? (message === CROSS_SITE_REFUSED ? "<p>Nothing was changed. To make this change, open this app and use its own page.</p>" : "<p>Ask whoever runs this app to give you a role.</p>") : ""}`), "text/html; charset=utf-8");
  });
});
store.init().then(
  () => server.listen({ port: PORT, host: LISTEN_ADDRESS }, () => console.log(`${APP_NAME} ${VERSION} listening on :${server.address().port} (requests kept in ${store.kind})`)),
  (err) => {
    console.error(`${err.message}\nDATABASE_URL is set, so this app will not start without its database.`);
    process.exit(1);
  },
);
```

It worked when both files parse. This prints nothing and exits 0:

```bash
node --check server.js && node --check store.js
```

```diff
 // The people you can sign in as locally. Change these to your app's own roles:

 const USERS = {
```

## 6. Add the test

Save this as `test/approvals.js`. It proves who can do what in both directions: each refused case has an allowed case beside it, so a check that can only ever refuse cannot pass by accident. It checks the role rule with a second requester, because the owner of a request is refused for two reasons at once.

```js
// test/approvals.js: `node test/approvals.js`. Proves who can do what, in BOTH directions:
// every "refused" row has an "allowed" row beside it, so the check can fail.
// Set TEST_DATABASE_URL to an EMPTY scratch Postgres database to run it against the database too.
const { spawn } = require("node:child_process");
const http = require("node:http");
const path = require("node:path");
const { SignJWT } = require("jose");
const { startMockPortal, USERS } = require("../dev/mock-portal");

const APP_ID = "app_approvals_test";
let pass = 0, fail = 0;
function check(name, got, want) {
  const ok = JSON.stringify(got) === JSON.stringify(want);
  ok ? pass++ : fail++;
  console.log(`${ok ? "ok  " : "FAIL"} ${name}${ok ? "" : `  (expected ${JSON.stringify(want)}, got ${JSON.stringify(got)})`}`);
}

(async () => {
  const portal = await startMockPortal({ port: 0, appId: APP_ID, as: "requester" });
  const child = spawn(process.execPath, [path.join(__dirname, "..", "server.js")], {
    env: { PATH: process.env.PATH, PORT: "0", LISTEN_ADDRESS: "127.0.0.1", VMNODES_PORTAL_URL: portal.issuer, VMNODES_APP_ID: APP_ID, ...(process.env.TEST_DATABASE_URL ? { DATABASE_URL: process.env.TEST_DATABASE_URL } : {}) },
    stdio: ["ignore", "pipe", "inherit"],
  });
  const base = await new Promise((resolve) => child.stdout.on("data", (d) => { const m = String(d).match(/listening on :(\d+)/); if (m) resolve(`http://127.0.0.1:${m[1]}`); }));

  // Signs a token for one of the mock portal's people, the way the real gateway would. `over` changes claims;
  // `extra` adds request headers, and a string body is sent as it is.
  async function call(who, method, p, body, over = {}, extra = {}) {
    const u = { ...USERS[who], ...over };
    const token = await new SignJWT({ email: u.email, name: u.name, kind: u.kind, groups: u.groups, roles: u.roles })
      .setProtectedHeader({ alg: "RS256", kid: "local-dev" }).setSubject(u.sub).setIssuer(portal.issuer).setAudience(APP_ID)
      .setIssuedAt().setExpirationTime("5m").sign(portal.privateKey);
    return new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const req = http.request(base + p, { method, headers: { "x-vmnodes-identity": token, "content-type": "application/json", ...extra } }, (res) => {
        let data = ""; res.on("data", (c) => (data += c));
        res.on("end", () => resolve({ status: res.statusCode, body: data, json: () => JSON.parse(data) }));
      });
      req.on("error", reject);
      if (body) req.write(typeof body === "string" ? body : JSON.stringify(body));
      req.end();
    });
  }

  // --- who may enter at all ---------------------------------------------------
  check("a person with neither role -> 403", (await call("nobody", "GET", "/api/requests")).status, 403);
  check("CONTROL: a requester gets in", (await call("requester", "GET", "/api/requests")).status, 200);

  // --- raising a request ------------------------------------------------------
  const made = await call("requester", "POST", "/api/requests", { item: "Standing desk <script>", amount: "249.9" });
  check("CONTROL: a requester can raise a request -> 201, pending, amount in pounds and pence", [made.status, made.json().status, made.json().amount], [201, "pending", "249.90"]);
  const id = made.json().id;
  check("an approver who is not a requester cannot raise one -> 403", (await call("approver", "POST", "/api/requests", { item: "Pens", amount: "5" })).status, 403);
  for (const amount of ["-5", "0", "abc", "12.345", "1e3", ""]) {
    check(`amount ${JSON.stringify(amount)} -> 400`, (await call("requester", "POST", "/api/requests", { item: "Pens", amount })).status, 400);
  }
  check("a missing item -> 400", (await call("requester", "POST", "/api/requests", { amount: "5" })).status, 400);

  // --- seeing: own records only, unless approver ---------------------------------
  check("the requester sees their own request", (await call("requester", "GET", "/api/requests")).json().items.map((r) => r.id), [id]);
  check("ANOTHER requester sees none of it", (await call("colleague", "GET", "/api/requests")).json().items, []);
  check("an approver sees every request", (await call("approver", "GET", "/api/requests")).json().items.map((r) => r.id), [id]);
  check("CONTROL: the owner can open it by id -> 200", (await call("requester", "GET", `/api/requests/${id}`)).status, 200);
  const other = await call("colleague", "GET", `/api/requests/${id}`);
  const missing = await call("colleague", "GET", "/api/requests/6f1c2a52-8f0d-4d64-9d0e-1c7b0e2a9b11");
  check("another requester opening it by id -> 404, the SAME answer as an id that does not exist", [other.status, other.body], [missing.status, missing.body]);
  check("a different person with the SAME EMAIL (different id) sees none of it: the key is id, not email", (await call("requester", "GET", "/api/requests", undefined, { sub: "usr_someone_else" })).json().items, []);

  // --- deciding: only approvers, and every time -------------------------------
  check("the requester cannot approve their own request -> 403 (the role check and the own-request rule both refuse this one)", (await call("requester", "POST", `/api/requests/${id}/decision`, { decision: "approve" })).status, 403);
  check("ANOTHER requester cannot approve -> 403 (only the role check can refuse this one)", (await call("colleague", "POST", `/api/requests/${id}/decision`, { decision: "approve" })).status, 403);
  check("...and nothing changed", (await call("approver", "GET", `/api/requests/${id}`)).json().status, "pending");
  check("a decision that is neither approve nor reject -> 400", (await call("approver", "POST", `/api/requests/${id}/decision`, { decision: "maybe" })).status, 400);
  check("a made-up request id -> 404", (await call("approver", "POST", "/api/requests/6f1c2a52-8f0d-4d64-9d0e-1c7b0e2a9b11/decision", { decision: "approve" })).status, 404);
  const rejected = await call("approver", "POST", `/api/requests/${id}/decision`, { decision: "reject", note: "Over budget" });
  check("CONTROL: an approver can reject -> 200, with the reason", [rejected.status, rejected.json().status, rejected.json().note, rejected.json().decidedByName], [200, "rejected", "Over budget", "Avery Approver"]);
  check("deciding twice -> 409, the first decision stands", [(await call("approver", "POST", `/api/requests/${id}/decision`, { decision: "approve" })).status, (await call("requester", "GET", `/api/requests/${id}`)).json().status], [409, "rejected"]);

  // --- nobody decides their own request -----------------------------------------
  const mine = (await call("both", "POST", "/api/requests", { item: "Monitor", amount: "180" })).json().id;
  check("someone who holds both roles cannot decide their own request -> 403", (await call("both", "POST", `/api/requests/${mine}/decision`, { decision: "approve" })).status, 403);
  check("...but another approver can -> 200", (await call("approver", "POST", `/api/requests/${mine}/decision`, { decision: "approve" })).status, 200);

  // --- the page: text is escaped, buttons follow the role ------------------------
  const asReq = await call("requester", "GET", "/");
  check("typed text is escaped, not run as markup", asReq.body.includes("Standing desk &lt;script&gt;") && !asReq.body.includes("<script>"), true);
  check("a requester's page has no Approve button", asReq.body.includes(">Approve<"), false);
  const second = (await call("colleague", "POST", "/api/requests", { item: "Chair", amount: "99" })).json().id;
  check("CONTROL: an approver's page has an Approve button for a pending request", (await call("approver", "GET", "/")).body.includes(`/requests/${second}/decision`), true);

  // --- changes sent from another site are refused, whoever is signed in ---------
  // A form on another app's page must not raise a request as the signed-in person.
  const formPost = (extra) => call("requester", "POST", "/requests", "item=From+elsewhere&amount=5", {}, { "content-type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", ...extra });
  const viaBrowser = async (extra) => (await formPost(extra)).status;
  check("a form post from ANOTHER site -> 403", await viaBrowser({ "sec-fetch-site": "cross-site" }), 403);
  const refusal = (await formPost({ "sec-fetch-site": "cross-site" })).body;
  check("the refusal page says nothing was changed, and does not say a role is missing", [refusal.includes("Nothing was changed"), refusal.includes("Ask whoever runs this app")], [true, false]);
  check("a form post from a SIBLING app on the same site -> 403", await viaBrowser({ "sec-fetch-site": "same-site" }), 403);
  check("a post with a foreign Origin and no fetch metadata -> 403", await viaBrowser({ origin: "https://evil.example" }), 403);
  const crossSiteRequests = (await call("requester", "GET", "/api/requests")).json().items.filter((r) => r.item === "From elsewhere").length;
  check("...and none of those three posts was saved", crossSiteRequests, 0);
  check("CONTROL: the app's own form (same-origin) still posts -> 303", await viaBrowser({ "sec-fetch-site": "same-origin" }), 303);

  const FLOOR = 31;
  if (pass + fail < FLOOR) { console.log(`FAIL only ${pass + fail} checks ran, expected at least ${FLOOR}`); fail++; }
  console.log(`\npassed=${pass} failed=${fail}`);
  child.kill(); portal.server.close();
  process.exit(fail === 0 ? 0 : 1);
})().catch((e) => { console.error("test crashed:", e); process.exit(1); });
```

```bash
npm test
```

It worked when the last line is `passed=35 failed=0`. To run it against the database as well, give it an empty scratch Postgres database ([Test with a scratch database](test-with-a-scratch-database.md) starts one): `TEST_DATABASE_URL=postgres://localhost/approvals_scratch npm test`.


Open `http://127.0.0.1:4100`.

It worked when the page is headed **Purchase requests**, reads "Signed in as Riley Requester", shows **What do you need?**, **Cost** and **Send request**, and has a table headed **Your requests**. Raise a request: the row shows "Waiting" and no **Approve** button, because you cannot decide your own.

Now switch person. Open `http://127.0.0.1:4100/_as/colleague`: the table is empty, because Casey did not raise it. Open `http://127.0.0.1:4100/_as/approver`: the page reads "Signed in as Avery Approver (approver)", the table is headed **All requests**, and the row has a reason box with **Approve** and **Reject**.
