<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/api/reading.md -->

# Reading shared data

Discover, describe and query the entities other apps share, ask a question in plain language, and pin the answers as charts. What a caller sees is decided by data grants, not by the request. An entity with no grant for the caller is invisible. A grant is created with POST /v1/data/grants by a caller holding an administrator-scoped API token for your org. The portal cannot issue API tokens or create grants today, even for an org administrator, so ask your VMnodes contact to create the grant and to give your app its token.

## List entities

`GET /v1/data/entities`

Lists the shared entities the caller can discover, with the fields the caller may see and the actions the caller holds. An entity the caller can discover but not read carries a `note`.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/data/entities" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "entity": "quotes.quote",
    "version": 1,
    "description": "A quote sent to a customer",
    "classification": "internal",
    "actions": [
      "discover",
      "read",
      "query",
      "aggregate"
    ],
    "fields": [
      {
        "name": "quoteNumber",
        "type": "string"
      },
      {
        "name": "customer",
        "type": "string"
      },
      {
        "name": "total",
        "type": "number"
      },
      {
        "name": "sentAt",
        "type": "timestamp"
      }
    ],
    "retired": false
  },
  {
    "entity": "visits.visit",
    "version": 1,
    "description": "A visitor sign-in",
    "classification": "internal",
    "actions": [
      "discover"
    ],
    "fields": [],
    "retired": false,
    "note": "You can see this exists. Ask its owner for access to read it."
  }
]
```

An app's own token works here and sees only what its grants allow. `retired` is true once the owner stops sharing the entity.

## Describe an entity

`GET /v1/data/entities/{entity}`

Returns one entity's definition: version, description, classification, source and the fields the caller may see.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `entity` | path | yes | The entity name, `<appName>.<local>`, for example `quotes.quote`. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/data/entities/<entity>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "entity": "quotes.quote",
  "version": 1,
  "description": "A quote sent to a customer",
  "classification": "internal",
  "source": "quotes",
  "vmnodesOwned": false,
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "quoteNumber",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "name": "customer",
      "type": "string"
    },
    {
      "name": "total",
      "type": "number"
    },
    {
      "name": "sentAt",
      "type": "timestamp"
    }
  ],
  "retired": false
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |

An unknown entity and an entity the caller has no grant for answer identically with 404.

## Query an entity

`POST /v1/data/query`

Runs one governed query. Name the fields to return in `select`. Filters are ANDed. Add `aggregate` to count, sum, min or max, optionally grouped. Each row carries `_provenance`, and the response says how fresh the data is and whether it was cut short.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/data/query" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"entity":"quotes.quote","select":["quoteNumber","customer","total"],"filter":[{"field":"total","op":"gte","value":1000}],"orderBy":{"field":"total","dir":"desc"},"limit":2}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "entity": "quotes.quote",
  "select": [
    "quoteNumber",
    "customer",
    "total"
  ],
  "filter": [
    {
      "field": "total",
      "op": "gte",
      "value": 1000
    }
  ],
  "orderBy": {
    "field": "total",
    "dir": "desc"
  },
  "limit": 2
}
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "rows": [
    {
      "quoteNumber": "Q-1042",
      "customer": "Example Pty Ltd",
      "total": 1850,
      "_provenance": {
        "sourceRef": "5d41402abc4b2a76b9719d911017c592e2b7a0c3f4d6e8a1b9c0d2e4f6a8b0c1",
        "lastSeenAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z"
      }
    }
  ],
  "provenance": {
    "entity": "quotes.quote/v1",
    "source": "quotes",
    "freshestAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
    "stalestAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z"
  },
  "truncated": false,
  "truncation": "none",
  "rowCount": 1
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 422 | `data/denied` | `no query access to '<entity>'` |
| 422 | `data/field-denied` | `field '<field>' is not available to you on '<entity>'` |
| 422 | `data/grain-not-readable` | `rows of '<entity>' are identified by <grain>, and <hidden> <is\|are> not available to you — two rows could differ in a way you cannot see. Aggregate instead (count, sum, min, max), which needs no row identity.` |
| 422 | `data/bad-op` | `unknown operator '<op>'` |
| 422 | `data/no-select` | `select is required — select at least one field` |
| 422 | `data/bad-entity` | `entity is required and must be a string` |
| 422 | `data/bad-select` | `select must be an array of field names` |
| 422 | `data/bad-filter` | `'in' needs 1-100 values` |
| 422 | `data/bad-order-by` | `orderBy.dir must be 'asc' or 'desc' when given` |
| 422 | `data/bad-aggregate` | `aggregate.fn must be one of count, sum, min, max` |
| 422 | `data/bad-limit` | `limit must be a positive integer` |
| 403 | `auth/on-behalf-of-not-permitted` | `only an application may act on behalf of a user` |

`filter[].op` is one of `eq`, `ne`, `in` (1 to 100 values), `gt`, `gte`, `lt`, `lte`, `contains`. `limit` defaults to 50 and is at most 200. `orderBy.dir` defaults to ascending. `aggregate` is `{fn, field?, groupBy?, buckets?}` with `fn` one of `count`, `sum`, `min`, `max`; a grouped aggregate returns rows such as `{"customer":"Example Pty Ltd","sum":1850}` and caps at 200 groups. `truncation` is `none`, `groups` or `scan`. `withheld` appears when the caller's grant hides fields or rows. Where the message above shows one example, the same code has sibling messages that name the field or operator at fault: `data/denied` also reads `no aggregate access to '<entity>'` for an aggregate; `data/no-select` also reads `select at least one field`; `data/bad-filter` also covers a `filter` that is not an array, an entry that is not an object, and an entry missing `field`, `op` or `value`; `data/bad-aggregate` also covers `aggregate` that is not an object, a `field` that is not a string, a `groupBy` that is not an array and `buckets` that are not `day`, `month` or `year`. An unknown entity, an entity with no grant and an entity with no shared fields all answer with the same `data/denied`, on purpose. An app can read for a signed-in person by sending that person's gateway identity token in the `X-Vmnodes-On-Behalf-Of` header; the query then runs with that person's access, and a token that is not valid for the app returns 403 `identity/on-behalf-of-invalid` with the message `identity token not valid for this application: <jose error>`. Only an app's own token may send the header. The `sourceRef` is an opaque value for this reader: do not parse it.

## Ask a question

`POST /v1/data/ask`

Asks one business question in plain language. The platform plans a constrained query from the caller's grants, runs it through the governed data path, and returns a cited answer with the exact plan that ran.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/data/ask" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"question":"What is the total value of quotes sent this month, by customer?"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "question": "What is the total value of quotes sent this month, by customer?"
}
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "answer": "Example Pty Ltd has 1850 in quotes this month; Sample Co has 420.5.",
  "queries": [
    {
      "plan": {
        "entity": "quotes.quote",
        "select": [
          "customer"
        ],
        "aggregate": {
          "fn": "sum",
          "field": "total",
          "groupBy": [
            "customer"
          ]
        }
      },
      "rows": [
        {
          "customer": "Example Pty Ltd",
          "sum": 1850
        },
        {
          "customer": "Sample Co",
          "sum": 420.5
        }
      ],
      "provenance": {
        "entity": "quotes.quote/v1",
        "source": "quotes",
        "freshestAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
        "stalestAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z"
      },
      "rowCount": 2,
      "truncated": false,
      "truncation": "none"
    }
  ],
  "plan": {
    "entity": "quotes.quote",
    "select": [
      "customer"
    ],
    "aggregate": {
      "fn": "sum",
      "field": "total",
      "groupBy": [
        "customer"
      ]
    }
  },
  "rows": [
    {
      "customer": "Example Pty Ltd",
      "sum": 1850
    },
    {
      "customer": "Sample Co",
      "sum": 420.5
    }
  ],
  "provenance": {
    "entity": "quotes.quote/v1",
    "source": "quotes",
    "freshestAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
    "stalestAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z"
  },
  "truncated": false,
  "rowCount": 2,
  "model": "example-model"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 501 | `ask/not-configured` | `natural-language queries are not configured on this control plane` |

`answer` is model-written, so the example answer is illustrative; the numbers come from `rows`. `queries` holds every query that ran, one per entity, because a question across two entities needs one query each. `plan`, `rows`, `provenance`, `truncated`, `truncation` and `rowCount` repeat the first query flat. `requestedChart` and `proposals` appear only when the question asked for a chart or for something to happen. Response shape not yet documented for `proposals` and `requestedChart`. A proposal is a request awaiting approval: nothing has happened until a person approves it. `question` is 1 to 2000 characters. Other 422 codes: `ask/bad-question`, `ask/no-data-access`, `ask/model-failed`, `ask/too-many-queries`, `ask/bad-plan`. A portal session may also call this route.

## List pinned charts

`GET /v1/data/pins`

Lists the caller's pinned charts, each re-run now as the caller, so a chart never shows more than the caller may see.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/data/pins" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "pins": [
    {
      "id": "pin_01JBX3G8NNBHKBVKS3CEH95TW0",
      "title": "Quote value by customer",
      "question": "What is the total value of quotes by customer?",
      "plan": {
        "entity": "quotes.quote",
        "select": [
          "customer"
        ],
        "aggregate": {
          "fn": "sum",
          "field": "total",
          "groupBy": [
            "customer"
          ]
        }
      },
      "chartKind": "bars",
      "position": 0,
      "createdAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
      "rows": [
        {
          "customer": "Example Pty Ltd",
          "sum": 1850
        }
      ],
      "rowCount": 1,
      "truncated": false,
      "truncation": "none",
      "provenance": {
        "entity": "quotes.quote/v1",
        "source": "quotes",
        "freshestAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
        "stalestAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z"
      },
      "unavailable": false
    }
  ]
}
```

Pins belong to one user. `unavailable` is true when the caller can no longer read the data behind a chart. A portal session may also call this route.

## Pin a chart

`POST /v1/data/pins`

Saves a grouped aggregate as a chart on the caller's dashboard. The `plan` is the plan returned by the ask call.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/data/pins" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"title":"Quote value by customer","question":"What is the total value of quotes by customer?","plan":{"entity":"quotes.quote","select":["customer"],"aggregate":{"fn":"sum","field":"total","groupBy":["customer"]}},"chartKind":"bars"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "title": "Quote value by customer",
  "question": "What is the total value of quotes by customer?",
  "plan": {
    "entity": "quotes.quote",
    "select": [
      "customer"
    ],
    "aggregate": {
      "fn": "sum",
      "field": "total",
      "groupBy": [
        "customer"
      ]
    }
  },
  "chartKind": "bars"
}
```

**Response** `201`

```json
{
  "id": "pin_01JBX3G8NNBHKBVKS3CEH95TW0"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 422 | `pins/no-question` | `a pin needs the question it answers` |
| 422 | `pins/not-chartable` | `only a grouped aggregate can be pinned as a chart` |
| 422 | `pins/full` | `a dashboard holds 24 charts — remove one first` |

`title` is optional and is cut to 120 characters. `chartKind` is optional and uses the chart names the ask call reports in `requestedChart`: `bars`, `stacked`, `grouped`, `line`, `pie` or `radar`. A user holds at most 24 pins. A portal session may also call this route.

## Remove a pinned chart

`DELETE /v1/data/pins/{id}`

Removes one of the caller's pinned charts.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | yes | The pin id, from the list of pinned charts. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X DELETE "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/data/pins/<id>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "removed": true
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `pins/not-found` | `no such pinned chart` |

A portal session may also call this route.

# Identity and the app directory

Apps that sign people in verify a gateway-issued identity token against the public keys below, and can invite customers or look up people through the directory calls. Directory calls need the matching scope on the app's token, which the manifest `permissions.directory` block requests.

## Get the identity public keys

`GET /auth/jwks`

Returns the public keys that verify the identity tokens the gateway issues. Cache the keys and refetch when a token names a `kid` you do not hold. This route is at the root of the API address, not under `/v1`.

**Auth:** none.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/auth/jwks"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "keys": [
    {
      "kty": "RSA",
      "n": "0vx7agoebGcQSuuPiLJXZptN9nndrQmbXEps2aiAFbWhM78LhWx4cbbfAAtVT86zwu1RK7aPFFxuhDR1L6tSoc_BJECPebWKRXjBZCiFV4n3oknjhMstn64tZ_2W-5JsGY4Hc5n9yBXArwl93lqt7_RN5w6Cf0h4QyQ5v-65YGjQR0_FDW2QvzqY368QQMicAtaSqzs8KJZgnYb9c7d0zgdAZHzu6qMQvRL5hajrn1n91CbOpbISD08qNLyrdkt-bFTWhAI4vMQFh6WeZu0fM4lFd2NcRwr3XPksINHaQ-G_xBniIqbw0Ls1jF44-csFCur-kEgU8awapJzKnqDKgw",
      "e": "AQAB",
      "kid": "key_01JBX3WP08XKV737QED1DQE8GP",
      "alg": "RS256",
      "use": "sig"
    }
  ]
}
```

Identity tokens are RS256 JWTs. Each key has `use` of `sig`.

## Invite a customer

`POST /v1/directory/customers`

Creates a customer identity entitled to one app and emails them an invite. The same email can be invited again to a different app. A customer is a separate kind of user from staff.

**Auth:** API token with the directory.invite-customers scope.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/directory/customers" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"email":"pat@example.com","displayName":"Pat Example","applicationId":"app_00000000000000000000000001"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "email": "pat@example.com",
  "displayName": "Pat Example",
  "applicationId": "app_00000000000000000000000001"
}
```

**Response** `201`

```json
{
  "userId": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
  "entitled": true
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `directory/forbidden` | `token lacks the directory.invite-customers scope` |
| 400 | `directory/no-application` | `applicationId is required` |
| 400 | `directory/foreign-application` | `a workload token invites customers to its own application only` |
| 400 | `directory/unknown-application` | `application does not exist in this organisation` |
| 400 | `directory/bad-email` | `invalid email address` |
| 400 | `directory/kind-conflict` | `a <kind> user already exists with this email` |

`displayName` is optional. An app's own token is pinned to its own app, so `applicationId` can be left out when the app calls; an administrator API token must send it. `kind` in the last error is the existing user's kind, for example `staff`.

## Look up people

`GET /v1/directory/lookup`

Searches the organisation's people for the calling app, matching a name or email fragment. Only people entitled to the app are returned. Only an app's own token can call it.

**Auth:** API token with the directory.lookup scope.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/directory/lookup?q=pat&limit=20" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "userId": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
    "displayName": "Pat Example",
    "email": "pat@example.com",
    "kind": "staff"
  }
]
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `directory/forbidden` | `token lacks the directory.lookup scope — declare permissions.directory.lookupPeople in the manifest` |
| 400 | `directory/no-application` | `a directory lookup is scoped to one application` |
| 400 | `directory/foreign-application` | `unknown application in this organisation` |

`limit` defaults to 20 and is held between 1 and 50.

## List groups for an app

`GET /v1/directory/groups`

Lists the groups attached to the calling app, for an app that shows or filters by group membership.

**Auth:** API token with the directory.group-members scope.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/directory/groups" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "groups": [
    {
      "groupId": "grp_01JBX3AEWFGRGNRHA3GTM6Y8FZ",
      "name": "sales-team"
    }
  ],
  "truncated": false
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `directory/forbidden` | `token lacks the directory.group-members scope — declare permissions.directory.listGroupMembers in the manifest` |

Needs an app's own token.

## List members of a group

`GET /v1/directory/groups/{groupId}/members`

Lists up to 1000 members of a group attached to the calling app. `truncated` is true when more exist.

**Auth:** API token with the directory.group-members scope.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groupId` | path | yes | The group id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/directory/groups/<groupId>/members" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "members": [
    {
      "userId": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
      "displayName": "Pat Example",
      "kind": "staff"
    }
  ],
  "truncated": false
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `directory/forbidden` | `token lacks the directory.group-members scope — declare permissions.directory.listGroupMembers in the manifest` |
| 404 | `directory/group-not-found` | `group does not exist` |

A group that is missing, in another organisation, or not attached to the app all answer 404.

<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/api/applications.md -->

# Applications and deployments

Create an app, build or register an image, deploy it to an environment, roll it back, stop and start it, read its configuration, logs and diagnosis, and provision its database. Every app has a `staging` and a `production` environment. Deployments are immutable and pinned to an image digest.

## List applications

`GET /v1/applications`

Lists the organisation's applications with a one-word status.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "id": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
    "name": "quotes",
    "displayName": "Quotes",
    "type": "web",
    "hostId": "host_00000000000000000000000003",
    "status": "active"
  }
]
```

`status` is `active`, `failed` or `never deployed`.

## Create an application

`POST /v1/applications`

Creates an app on the organisation's host and gives it a `staging` and a `production` environment. Nothing runs until you deploy.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"name":"quotes","port":3000,"displayName":"Quotes","type":"web","resourceProfile":"standard","healthEndpoint":"/health"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "name": "quotes",
  "port": 3000,
  "displayName": "Quotes",
  "type": "web",
  "resourceProfile": "standard",
  "healthEndpoint": "/health"
}
```

**Response** `201`

```json
{
  "id": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
  "organisationId": "org_00000000000000000000000004",
  "hostId": "host_00000000000000000000000003",
  "name": "quotes",
  "displayName": "Quotes",
  "type": "web",
  "port": 3000,
  "resourceProfile": "standard",
  "accessProfile": "company",
  "healthEndpoint": "/health",
  "databaseEnabled": false,
  "persistentStorage": false,
  "telemetryProfile": "standard",
  "createdAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 422 | `app/invalid-manifest` | `name and port are required` |
| 422 | `app/reserved-name` | `That name is reserved.` |
| 422 | `app/no-host` | `no healthy host with a live node available` |
| 422 | `app/name-taken` | `You already have an app called <name>. Choose a different name.` |

`name` and `port` are required. `type` is `web`, `api`, `worker`, `scheduled-job` or `mcp-server`. `resourceProfile` is `tiny`, `standard`, `large`, `compute` or `custom` and defaults to `standard`. `hostId` is optional and defaults to the organisation's host. A name that is too long returns 422 `app/name-too-long`.

## Get an application

`GET /v1/applications/{appId}`

Returns one application.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "id": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
  "organisationId": "org_00000000000000000000000004",
  "hostId": "host_00000000000000000000000003",
  "name": "quotes",
  "displayName": "Quotes",
  "type": "web",
  "port": 3000,
  "resourceProfile": "standard",
  "accessProfile": "company",
  "healthEndpoint": "/health",
  "databaseEnabled": false,
  "persistentStorage": false,
  "telemetryProfile": "standard",
  "createdAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
  "updatedAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |

## Build an image from git

`POST /v1/applications/{appId}/builds`

Builds the repository at a public git URL into an image and returns its digest. The repository needs a `Dockerfile`. The digest is registered for this app, ready to deploy.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/builds" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"source":{"kind":"git","url":"https://github.com/example/quotes.git","ref":"main"}}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "source": {
    "kind": "git",
    "url": "https://github.com/example/quotes.git",
    "ref": "main"
  }
}
```

**Response** `201`

```json
{
  "imageDigest": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a",
  "undeclaredTemplateRoles": []
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |
| 403 | `build/path-source-disabled` | `path sources are disabled on this control plane; build from a git URL` |

`ref` is optional. A failed build returns 422 with a code and a message naming the cause. The response can also carry `fetchPath`. `undeclaredTemplateRoles` lists permission-template roles the app uses but its manifest does not declare.

## Register an image digest

`POST /v1/applications/{appId}/images`

Registers an image you built elsewhere so it can be deployed. Send a full digest reference.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/images" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"digest":"registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a","gitCommit":"4c1d9e07a35b82f6d0e1c4b97a52f3860de1b7c9"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "digest": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a",
  "gitCommit": "4c1d9e07a35b82f6d0e1c4b97a52f3860de1b7c9"
}
```

**Response** `201`

```json
{
  "imageDigest": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |
| 422 | `deploy/placeholder-digest` | `image is the release placeholder, not a built digest — the all-zero digest is well-formed enough to pass a shape check and to sign, and fails only at pull. Register the digest from the signing commit, not the tagged one.` |
| 422 | `deploy/bad-digest` | `image must be a digest reference: <registry>/<repo>[:tag]@sha256:<64 hex>` |
| 422 | `deploy/bad-git-commit` | `gitCommit must be the full 40-character lowercase hex sha — got '<value>'. An abbreviated or otherwise malformed commit is refused, not stored: a stored abbreviation invites prefix comparison later, and prefix comparison is label-matching.` |

`gitCommit` is optional. When sent it must be the full 40-character commit.

## List environments

`GET /v1/applications/{appId}/environments`

Lists an app's environments. Use it to turn `staging` or `production` into an environment id.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/environments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "id": "env_00000000000000000000000005",
    "applicationId": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
    "name": "staging",
    "isProduction": false,
    "createdAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
    "stoppedAt": null,
    "stoppedBy": null
  },
  {
    "id": "env_00000000000000000000000006",
    "applicationId": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
    "name": "production",
    "isProduction": true,
    "createdAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
    "stoppedAt": null,
    "stoppedBy": null
  }
]
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |

`stoppedAt` and `stoppedBy` are set while the environment is stopped, otherwise null.

## Deploy an image

`POST /v1/applications/{appId}/deployments`

Starts a deployment of an image digest to an environment. The call returns at once with status `deploying`; poll the deployments list for `active` or `failed`. A deployment that fails its health check does not take traffic.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/deployments" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"environmentId":"env_00000000000000000000000006","imageDigest":"registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "environmentId": "env_00000000000000000000000006",
  "imageDigest": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a"
}
```

**Response** `202`

```json
{
  "id": "dep_00000000000000000000000007",
  "applicationId": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
  "environmentId": "env_00000000000000000000000006",
  "imageDigest": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a",
  "createdBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
  "status": "deploying",
  "startedAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |
| 422 | `deploy/env-not-found` | `no environment <environmentId>` |
| 422 | `deploy/unknown-image` | `image digest not in registry metadata — build first` |
| 422 | `deploy/scan-gate` | `image scan status is '<status>' — refused regardless of the scan gate mode` |
| 422 | `deploy/host-not-ready` | `no ready node on the application's host` |

Deployment `status` is `pending`, `building`, `deploying`, `validating`, `active`, `failed`, `rolled-back` or `superseded`. Other 422 codes: `deploy/image-withdrawn`, `deploy/no-address`, `deploy/agent-too-old`, `deploy/no-service`, and database codes when the app's database is not ready. A scan that blocks the deploy can also say `the scan gate blocks this deploy` in the same code.

## List deployments

`GET /v1/applications/{appId}/deployments`

Lists up to 50 deployments of one environment, newest first.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/deployments?environmentId=env_00000000000000000000000006" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "id": "dep_00000000000000000000000007",
    "applicationId": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
    "environmentId": "env_00000000000000000000000006",
    "imageDigest": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a",
    "createdBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
    "status": "deploying",
    "startedAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z"
  },
  {
    "id": "dep_00000000000000000000000008",
    "applicationId": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
    "environmentId": "env_00000000000000000000000006",
    "imageDigest": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a",
    "createdBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
    "status": "superseded",
    "startedAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
    "completedAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z"
  }
]
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |
| 400 | `deployments/environment-required` | `environmentId query parameter is required` |

`environmentId` is required. A deployment may also carry `previousDeploymentId`, `failureReason` and `viaAgent`.

## Roll back

`POST /v1/applications/{appId}/rollback`

Rolls an environment back to its previous known-good deployment, or to a named one. The rollback is itself a new deployment of the older image.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/rollback" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"environmentId":"env_00000000000000000000000006","toDeploymentId":"dep_00000000000000000000000008"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "environmentId": "env_00000000000000000000000006",
  "toDeploymentId": "dep_00000000000000000000000008"
}
```

**Response** `202`

```json
{
  "id": "dep_00000000000000000000000007",
  "applicationId": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
  "environmentId": "env_00000000000000000000000006",
  "imageDigest": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a",
  "createdBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
  "status": "deploying",
  "startedAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
  "previousDeploymentId": "dep_00000000000000000000000007"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |
| 422 | `rollback/no-target` | `no previous deployment to roll back to` |

`toDeploymentId` is optional. A portal session may also call this route.

## Stop an environment

`POST /v1/applications/{appId}/environments/{environmentId}/stop`

Pauses an environment by stopping its container. Reversible: start redeploys the same image. It frees CPU and memory on the host.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |
| `environmentId` | path | yes | The environment id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/environments/<environmentId>/stop" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `202`

```json
{
  "stoppedAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
  "stoppedBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |
| 403 | `environment/permission-denied` | `stopping or starting an application needs an organisation administrator, or the application's admin or owner role` |
| 404 | `environment/not-found` | `no environment <environmentId>` |
| 409 | `environment/stop-conflict` | `this environment is already stopped` |

The caller must be an organisation administrator or hold the app's admin or owner role.

## Start an environment

`POST /v1/applications/{appId}/environments/{environmentId}/start`

Resumes a stopped environment by redeploying the image it was running. The deploy gates apply again, so a build the scan now refuses cannot be restarted.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |
| `environmentId` | path | yes | The environment id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/environments/<environmentId>/start" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `202`

```json
{
  "id": "dep_00000000000000000000000007",
  "applicationId": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
  "environmentId": "env_00000000000000000000000006",
  "imageDigest": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a",
  "createdBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
  "status": "deploying",
  "startedAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |
| 403 | `environment/permission-denied` | `stopping or starting an application needs an organisation administrator, or the application's admin or owner role` |
| 404 | `environment/not-found` | `no environment <environmentId>` |
| 409 | `environment/start-conflict` | `this environment is not stopped; there is nothing to start` |
| 422 | `environment/no-deployment` | `this environment has never had a successful deployment to restart` |

The caller must be an organisation administrator or hold the app's admin or owner role.

## List configuration

`GET /v1/applications/{appId}/config`

Lists an environment's configuration entries. Values of secret entries are never returned.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/config?environmentId=env_00000000000000000000000006" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "name": "LOG_LEVEL",
    "isSecret": false,
    "removed": false,
    "version": 2,
    "setAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
    "inEffect": true,
    "value": "info"
  },
  {
    "name": "DATABASE_URL",
    "isSecret": true,
    "removed": false,
    "version": 1,
    "setAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
    "inEffect": true
  }
]
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |

`value` is present only when `isSecret` is false. `inEffect` is false until the entry reaches a running deployment.

## List secret names

`GET /v1/applications/{appId}/secrets`

Lists the names of an environment's secrets with their versions. Values are never returned.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/secrets?environmentId=env_00000000000000000000000006" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "name": "DATABASE_URL",
    "version": 1,
    "createdAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z"
  }
]
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |

## Provision the database

`POST /v1/applications/{appId}/database`

Provisions the app's own PostgreSQL database. It is safe to call again. `DATABASE_URL` is set as a secret in every environment and reaches the app on its next deploy.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/database" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `202`

```json
{
  "databaseId": "db_01JBX34A08YC14FXVWRVX8PVFT",
  "name": "quotes",
  "roleName": "app_quotes_user",
  "status": "provisioning"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |
| 422 | `db/name-conflict` | `host <hostId> already has a database named '<name>' (<dbId>), owned by application <appId>. Application names that normalise to the same identifier cannot share a host: rename one, or place it on another host. Nothing was provisioned.` |

The database name is the app name in lowercase with any character outside `a-z`, `0-9` and `_` replaced by `_`. `db/name-conflict` returns 422 when another app's database on the same host already has that name.

## List restore points

`GET /v1/databases/{dbId}/restore-points`

Lists the 20 most recent verified restore points for a database, newest first.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `dbId` | path | yes | The database id, from the database provisioning response. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/databases/<dbId>/restore-points" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "id": "rp_01JBX36K6RCQY1G9B7XF4DR5SB",
    "backupId": "bak_01JBX3FVAJCWG4HWPXX3847K8P",
    "databaseId": "db_01JBX34A08YC14FXVWRVX8PVFT",
    "verifiedAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
    "createdAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z"
  }
]
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |

## Read logs

`GET /v1/applications/{appId}/logs`

Reads recent log lines for an environment, optionally filtered by a substring.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/logs?environmentId=env_00000000000000000000000006&sinceMinutes=60&search=error&limit=100" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "lines": [
    {
      "timestamp": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
      "line": "error: connection refused to upstream"
    }
  ]
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |

`environmentId` is required. `sinceMinutes` defaults to 60 and `limit` to 100. `search` matches a substring.

## Diagnose an application

`GET /v1/applications/{appId}/diagnose`

Answers why an app is broken in one call: the latest deployment, node health, recent error lines and a plain summary.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `appId` | path | yes | The application id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/applications/<appId>/diagnose?environmentId=env_00000000000000000000000006" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "summary": "The latest deployment failed its health check: the app did not answer on port 3000.",
  "deployment": {
    "id": "dep_00000000000000000000000007",
    "status": "failed",
    "imageDigest": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a",
    "startedAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z"
  },
  "recentErrors": [
    "error: listen EADDRINUSE: address already in use :::3000"
  ],
  "node": {
    "status": "ready",
    "lastHeartbeatAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z"
  }
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |

`deployment` and `node` are left out when there is none. `environmentId` is required.

# People and roles

List the organisation's directory, flag organisation administrators, set managers, and read an app's roles. Customer identities are separate from staff identities and can never be organisation administrators.

## List users

`GET /v1/directory/users`

Lists every person in the organisation, staff and customers.

**Auth:** administrator (portal session or API token).

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/directory/users" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "userId": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
    "email": "pat@example.com",
    "displayName": "Pat Example",
    "kind": "staff",
    "isOrgAdmin": true,
    "managerUserId": null,
    "createdAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z"
  }
]
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `directory/forbidden` | `listing the directory needs an admin token, or an organisation administrator` |

## Set organisation administrator

`PUT /v1/directory/users/{userId}/org-admin`

Promotes or demotes a user as an organisation administrator. Administrators approve extension access to data, promote others and receive incident alerts.

**Auth:** administrator (portal session or API token).

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `userId` | path | yes | The user id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X PUT "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/directory/users/<userId>/org-admin" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"isOrgAdmin":true}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "isOrgAdmin": true
}
```

**Response** `204`

```json
null
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `directory/forbidden` | `flagging an organisation admin needs an organisation administrator, or an admin token` |
| 400 | `directory/unknown-user` | `user does not exist in this organisation` |
| 400 | `directory/customer-not-admin` | `customer identities cannot be organisation admins` |
| 409 | `directory/last-administrator` | `this is the only administrator of the organisation, and removing the last one cannot be undone from the console: nobody would be able to approve an extension's access to your data, promote a replacement, or receive incident alerts. Promote another administrator first, then remove this one. Nothing was changed.` |

Only `"isOrgAdmin": true` promotes. A body that leaves the field out or sends anything else demotes the user. Always send the field.

## Set a user's manager

`PUT /v1/directory/users/{userId}/manager`

Sets or clears who a user reports to.

**Auth:** administrator API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `userId` | path | yes | The user id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X PUT "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/directory/users/<userId>/manager" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"managerUserId":"usr_00000000000000000000000009"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "managerUserId": "usr_00000000000000000000000009"
}
```

**Response** `204`

```json
null
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `directory/forbidden` | `setting a manager requires an admin token` |
| 400 | `directory/self-manager` | `a user cannot be their own manager` |
| 400 | `directory/unknown-user` | `user does not exist in this organisation` |

Send `managerUserId` as `null`, or leave it out, to clear the manager.

## Related

- [API reference](index.md)
- [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md)

<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/api/groups.md -->

# Groups

Groups collect people so a data grant or an action grant can name them once. Group names are lowercase kebab-case.

## Create a group

`POST /v1/groups`

Creates a group in the organisation.

**Auth:** administrator (portal session or API token).

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/groups" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"name":"sales-team","description":"Everyone who sends quotes"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "name": "sales-team",
  "description": "Everyone who sends quotes"
}
```

**Response** `201`

```json
{
  "groupId": "grp_01JBX3AEWFGRGNRHA3GTM6Y8FZ",
  "name": "sales-team"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `directory/forbidden` | `creating a group needs an organisation administrator, or an admin token` |
| 422 | `identity/bad-group-name` | `group names are lowercase kebab-case, 2-49 characters` |
| 409 | `identity/group-name-conflict` | `a group named '<name>' already exists in this organisation` |

`description` is optional.

## Add a group member

`POST /v1/groups/{groupId}/members`

Adds a user to a group. Adding a user who is already a member succeeds.

**Auth:** administrator (portal session or API token).

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groupId` | path | yes | The group id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/groups/<groupId>/members" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"userId":"usr_00000000000000000000000002"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "userId": "usr_00000000000000000000000002"
}
```

**Response** `204`

```json
null
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `directory/forbidden` | `changing group membership needs an organisation administrator, or an admin token` |
| 422 | `identity/group-not-found` | `no group '<groupId>'` |
| 422 | `identity/user-not-found` | `no user '<userId>'` |

## Remove a group member

`DELETE /v1/groups/{groupId}/members/{userId}`

Removes a user from a group. Removing a user who is not a member also succeeds.

**Auth:** administrator (portal session or API token).

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `groupId` | path | yes | The group id. |
| `userId` | path | yes | The user id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X DELETE "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/groups/<groupId>/members/<userId>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `204`

```json
null
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `directory/forbidden` | `changing group membership needs an organisation administrator, or an admin token` |
| 422 | `identity/group-not-found` | `no group '<groupId>'` |

<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/api/governance.md -->

# Data governance

Data grants decide who may discover, read, query or aggregate a shared entity. Only an administrator API token can create one, so an app cannot widen its own access.

## Grant data access

`POST /v1/data/grants`

Lets one user, one group or one app discover, read, query or aggregate a shared entity. Name exactly one principal.

**Auth:** administrator API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/data/grants" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"entity":"quotes.quote","actions":["discover","read","query","aggregate"],"groupId":"grp_01JBX3AEWFGRGNRHA3GTM6Y8FZ","allowedFields":["quoteNumber","customer","total"],"maxRows":1000,"purpose":"Sales reporting","expiresDays":90}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "entity": "quotes.quote",
  "actions": [
    "discover",
    "read",
    "query",
    "aggregate"
  ],
  "groupId": "grp_01JBX3AEWFGRGNRHA3GTM6Y8FZ",
  "allowedFields": [
    "quoteNumber",
    "customer",
    "total"
  ],
  "maxRows": 1000,
  "purpose": "Sales reporting",
  "expiresDays": 90
}
```

**Response** `201`

```json
{
  "grantId": "dg_01JBX39BR2FQD1D451Z0SXWMWA"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `grants/forbidden-workload` | `an application's own token cannot grant access; an organisation administrator's admin token can` |
| 403 | `grants/forbidden-scope` | `granting requires the 'admin' scope` |
| 404 | `identity/not-found` | `no such resource` |
| 422 | `data/one-principal` | `exactly one of userId/groupId/applicationId is required` |
| 422 | `data/unknown-entity` | `no entity '<entity>' in this organisation` |

`actions` holds `discover`, `read`, `query` or `aggregate`. `allowedFields`, `recordScope`, `maxRows`, `purpose` and `expiresDays` are optional; leaving `allowedFields` out grants every shared field. A portal session cannot call this route. Ask your VMnodes contact for an administrator API token.

## Related

- [API reference](index.md)
- [Troubleshooting](../troubleshooting.md)

<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/api/actions.md -->

# Actions and approvals

Actions are the only write path across apps: a caller proposes a typed action, the action's approval policy decides whether it queues at once or waits for a different person to approve, and the result is polled by invocation id. Plans chain several actions behind one approval.

## List actions

`GET /v1/actions`

Lists the registered actions the caller may propose or approve, with each input schema, risk and approval policy.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/actions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "action": "quotes.send-quote",
    "version": 1,
    "description": "Email a quote to the customer",
    "risk": "moderate",
    "approvalPolicy": "required",
    "inputSchema": {
      "type": "object",
      "properties": {
        "quoteNumber": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      },
      "required": [
        "quoteNumber"
      ]
    },
    "derivedInputs": [],
    "canPropose": true,
    "canApprove": false
  }
]
```

`risk` is `low`, `moderate` or `high`. `approvalPolicy` is `none` or `required`. `derivedInputs` names inputs the platform fills in from governed data; a caller cannot supply them.

## Propose an action

`POST /v1/actions/propose`

Proposes one action. A low-risk, pre-authorised action queues at once; one that needs approval waits for a different person. Poll the invocation for the outcome.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/actions/propose" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"action":"quotes.send-quote","input":{"quoteNumber":"Q-1042"},"idempotencyKey":"send-Q-1042-2026-10-22"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "action": "quotes.send-quote",
  "input": {
    "quoteNumber": "Q-1042"
  },
  "idempotencyKey": "send-Q-1042-2026-10-22"
}
```

**Response** `202`

```json
{
  "invocationId": "inv_01JBX3VSJ2D3QV2Z0B17EQ78VS",
  "status": "proposed",
  "deduplicated": false
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 422 | `actions/denied` | `no propose access to '<action>'` |
| 422 | `actions/bad-input` | `input does not match the action schema: <detail>` |
| 422 | `actions/rate-limited` | `'<action>' allows <n> proposals per hour` |

`status` is `proposed` (waiting for approval) or `queued`. `input` defaults to an empty object. Always send an `idempotencyKey` you derive from the business event: without one every call is a new proposal and nothing is deduplicated. Supplying an input the platform derives returns 422 `actions/derived-input-supplied`.

## List actions awaiting approval

`GET /v1/actions/pending`

Lists proposals waiting for approval, limited to actions the caller may approve.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/actions/pending" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "invocationId": "inv_01JBX3VSJ2D3QV2Z0B17EQ78VS",
    "action": "quotes.send-quote",
    "risk": "moderate",
    "input": {
      "quoteNumber": "Q-1042"
    },
    "provenance": {},
    "description": "Email a quote to the customer",
    "compensation": null,
    "derivedInputs": [],
    "proposedBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
    "proposedAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z"
  }
]
```

Response shape not yet documented for `provenance`; the empty object in the example is a placeholder.

## Approve an action

`POST /v1/actions/{invocationId}/approve`

Approves a waiting proposal and queues it. The approver must be someone other than the proposer.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invocationId` | path | yes | The invocation id from the propose call. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/actions/<invocationId>/approve" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"reason":"Checked the total with the customer"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "reason": "Checked the total with the customer"
}
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "status": "queued"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `actions/not-found` | `no such invocation` |
| 422 | `actions/not-pending` | `invocation is '<status>', not awaiting approval` |
| 422 | `actions/denied` | `no approve access to '<action>'` |
| 422 | `actions/self-approval` | `the approver must be different from the proposer` |

`reason` is optional. A portal session may also call this route.

## Deny an action

`POST /v1/actions/{invocationId}/deny`

Denies a waiting proposal.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invocationId` | path | yes | The invocation id from the propose call. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/actions/<invocationId>/deny" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"reason":"Wrong customer"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "reason": "Wrong customer"
}
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "status": "denied"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `actions/not-found` | `no such invocation` |
| 422 | `actions/not-pending` | `invocation is '<status>', not awaiting approval` |
| 422 | `actions/denied` | `no approve access to '<action>'` |
| 422 | `actions/self-approval` | `the approver must be different from the proposer` |

`reason` is optional. A portal session may also call this route.

## Get an action invocation

`GET /v1/actions/{invocationId}`

Returns the status and result of one invocation. Only the proposer or someone who may approve the action can see it.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `invocationId` | path | yes | The invocation id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/actions/<invocationId>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "invocationId": "inv_01JBX3VSJ2D3QV2Z0B17EQ78VS",
  "action": "quotes.send-quote",
  "status": "succeeded",
  "input": {
    "quoteNumber": "Q-1042"
  },
  "provenance": {},
  "result": {
    "sent": true
  },
  "errorDetail": null,
  "proposedBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
  "approvedBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000009",
  "denyReason": null,
  "attempts": 1,
  "proposedAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
  "completedAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `actions/not-found` | `no such invocation` |

`status` is `proposed`, `queued`, `leased`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `denied` or `dead`. Anyone else gets 404. Response shape not yet documented for `provenance` and `result`, whose contents depend on the action; the examples are placeholders.

## Grant action access

`POST /v1/actions/grants`

Lets one user, one group or one app propose, or approve, an action. Name exactly one principal.

**Auth:** administrator API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/actions/grants" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"action":"quotes.send-quote","groupId":"grp_01JBX3AEWFGRGNRHA3GTM6Y8FZ","allowPropose":true,"allowApprove":false,"purpose":"Sales team sends quotes","expiresDays":90}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "action": "quotes.send-quote",
  "groupId": "grp_01JBX3AEWFGRGNRHA3GTM6Y8FZ",
  "allowPropose": true,
  "allowApprove": false,
  "purpose": "Sales team sends quotes",
  "expiresDays": 90
}
```

**Response** `201`

```json
{
  "grantId": "ag_01JBX3FS6TKPBWAAZHT7N83MS7"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `grants/forbidden-workload` | `an application's own token cannot grant access; an organisation administrator's admin token can` |
| 403 | `grants/forbidden-scope` | `granting requires the 'admin' scope` |
| 422 | `actions/one-principal` | `exactly one of userId/groupId/applicationId is required` |
| 422 | `actions/unknown-action` | `no action '<action>' in this organisation` |

`allowPropose` defaults to true and `allowApprove` to false. `purpose` and `expiresDays` are optional. A portal session cannot call this route.

## Propose a plan

`POST /v1/plans`

Proposes up to 20 actions as one plan that a person approves once. A step can use an earlier step's output with `{"$fromStep": 1, "output": "fieldName"}`.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/plans" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"name":"Onboard Sample Co","description":"Create the customer and send the first quote","steps":[{"action":"quotes.create-quote","input":{"customer":"Sample Co"}},{"action":"quotes.send-quote","input":{"quoteNumber":{"$fromStep":1,"output":"quoteNumber"}},"waitUntil":"2026-10-23T00:00:00.000Z","waitReason":"Send after the customer'\''s office opens"}]}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "name": "Onboard Sample Co",
  "description": "Create the customer and send the first quote",
  "steps": [
    {
      "action": "quotes.create-quote",
      "input": {
        "customer": "Sample Co"
      }
    },
    {
      "action": "quotes.send-quote",
      "input": {
        "quoteNumber": {
          "$fromStep": 1,
          "output": "quoteNumber"
        }
      },
      "waitUntil": "2026-10-23T00:00:00.000Z",
      "waitReason": "Send after the customer's office opens"
    }
  ]
}
```

**Response** `201`

```json
{
  "planId": "plan_01JBX3M08R69XJE166YVJK034H",
  "status": "proposed"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 422 | `plans/no-name` | `a plan needs a name` |
| 422 | `plans/empty` | `a plan needs at least one step` |
| 422 | `plans/too-long` | `a plan holds at most 20 steps` |
| 422 | `plans/step-denied` | `step <n>: no propose access to '<action>'` |
| 422 | `plans/bad-reference` | `step <n> field '<key>' refers to step <k>, which is not an earlier step — a reference can only name a step that has already run` |
| 422 | `plans/bad-wait` | `step <n>: waitUntil is not a valid timestamp` |
| 422 | `plans/bad-template-ref` | `templateRef is at most 200 characters` |

`description`, `templateRef`, `waitUntil` and `waitReason` are optional. The plan's steps run in order once approved.

## List plans

`GET /v1/plans`

Lists plans the caller proposed or may decide.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/plans" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "plans": [
    {
      "id": "plan_01JBX3M08R69XJE166YVJK034H",
      "name": "Onboard Sample Co",
      "description": "Create the customer and send the first quote",
      "status": "proposed",
      "templateRef": null,
      "proposedBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
      "approvedBy": null,
      "denyReason": null,
      "createdAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
      "completedAt": null,
      "steps": [
        {
          "id": "pstep_01JBX34AGQ80JJ4HDT8QY4V3PY",
          "position": 1,
          "action": "quotes.send-quote",
          "input": {
            "quoteNumber": "Q-1043"
          },
          "status": "pending",
          "invocationId": null,
          "result": null,
          "errorDetail": null,
          "description": "Email a quote to the customer",
          "risk": "moderate",
          "compensation": null,
          "waitUntil": null,
          "waitReason": null
        }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

## Get a plan

`GET /v1/plans/{id}`

Returns one plan with each step's status and result.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | yes | The plan id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/plans/<id>" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "id": "plan_01JBX3M08R69XJE166YVJK034H",
  "name": "Onboard Sample Co",
  "description": "Create the customer and send the first quote",
  "status": "proposed",
  "templateRef": null,
  "proposedBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
  "approvedBy": null,
  "denyReason": null,
  "createdAt": "2026-10-20T03:14:07.000Z",
  "completedAt": null,
  "steps": [
    {
      "id": "pstep_01JBX34AGQ80JJ4HDT8QY4V3PY",
      "position": 1,
      "action": "quotes.send-quote",
      "input": {
        "quoteNumber": "Q-1043"
      },
      "status": "pending",
      "invocationId": null,
      "result": null,
      "errorDetail": null,
      "description": "Email a quote to the customer",
      "risk": "moderate",
      "compensation": null,
      "waitUntil": null,
      "waitReason": null
    }
  ]
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `plans/not-found` | `no such plan` |

Plan `status` is `proposed`, `approved`, `running`, `completed`, `denied` or `failed`.

## Approve or deny a plan

`POST /v1/plans/{id}/decision`

Approves or denies a proposed plan. Approving needs approve access to every action in it, and the approver must be someone other than the proposer.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `id` | path | yes | The plan id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/plans/<id>/decision" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"decision":"approve","reason":"Reviewed the quote values"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "decision": "approve",
  "reason": "Reviewed the quote values"
}
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "status": "approved"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 400 | `plans/bad-decision` | `decision must be approve or deny` |
| 404 | `plans/not-found` | `no such plan` |
| 422 | `plans/not-pending` | `plan is '<status>', not awaiting approval` |
| 422 | `plans/self-approval` | `the approver must be different from the proposer` |
| 422 | `plans/step-not-approvable` | `you may not approve '<action>' (step <n>), so you cannot approve a plan containing it` |

`status` in the response is `approved` or `denied`. `reason` is optional. This route needs an API token: a portal session cannot call it.

# Connectors

Connectors link the organisation to outside systems. Setting one up is an operator step: ask your VMnodes contact.

## List connectors

`GET /v1/connectors`

Lists the organisation's connectors with their state.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/connectors" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "id": "conn_01JBX3K00ZAR68QNR66YFVTGS1",
    "kind": "xero",
    "status": "connected",
    "tenantName": "Example Pty Ltd",
    "lastSyncAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
    "lastError": null
  }
]
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 501 | `connector/not-configured` | `no connectors configured` |

## Sync Xero

`POST /v1/connectors/xero/sync`

Pulls contacts and invoices from the connected Xero organisation into the platform.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/connectors/xero/sync" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "contacts": 42,
  "invoices": 118,
  "lines": 307,
  "tenant": "Example Pty Ltd"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 501 | `connector/not-configured` | `Xero is not configured` |
| 422 | `xero/not-connected` | `connect Xero first` |
| 422 | `xero/disabled` | `the Xero connection is disabled` |

Connecting Xero is an operator step: ask your VMnodes contact.

<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/api/mail.md -->

# Mail

Send a plain-text email to a person in the organisation or to an address, from the platform's sending address. Needs the `mail.send` scope, which the manifest `permissions.mail.send` field requests.

## Send an email

`POST /v1/connectors/mail/send`

Sends a plain-text email to a person in the organisation or to an address. The idempotency key makes a retried call send once.

**Auth:** API token with the mail.send scope.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/connectors/mail/send" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"to":{"email":"pat@example.com"},"subject":"Quote Q-1042","textBody":"Hello Pat,\n\nYour quote Q-1042 is ready.","ref":"Q-1042","idempotencyKey":"quote-Q-1042-sent"}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "to": {
    "email": "pat@example.com"
  },
  "subject": "Quote Q-1042",
  "textBody": "Hello Pat,\n\nYour quote Q-1042 is ready.",
  "ref": "Q-1042",
  "idempotencyKey": "quote-Q-1042-sent"
}
```

**Response** `202`

```json
{
  "messageId": "mail_01JBX3GGZF4R91KTZVQGQ41EZX",
  "status": "sent"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `mail/forbidden` | `token lacks the mail.send scope` |
| 400 | `mail/bad-subject` | `subject is required (max 200 chars)` |
| 400 | `mail/bad-body` | `textBody is required (max 100000 chars)` |
| 400 | `mail/bad-idempotency-key` | `idempotencyKey is required (max 200 chars)` |
| 400 | `mail/bad-ref` | `ref must be a string (max 100 chars)` |
| 400 | `mail/bad-recipient` | `provide exactly one of to.userId or to.email` |
| 400 | `mail/unknown-recipient` | `no such user in this organisation` |
| 429 | `mail/rate-limited` | `hourly send limit reached` |
| 502 | `mail/send-failed` | `mail transport failed; retry with the same idempotencyKey` |

`to` holds exactly one of `userId` or `email`. `ref` is optional. An invalid address returns 400 `mail/bad-recipient` with `invalid email address`. When mail is not set up the 503 body is a bare `{"error":"mail transport is not configured"}` with no code. Limits: 50 sends per hour per caller and 200 per hour per organisation; a 429 carries a `retry-after` header of 300 seconds.

<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/api/ai.md -->

# AI completions

Run a model completion without holding model credentials. Needs the `ai.complete` scope, which the manifest `permissions.ai.complete` field requests. Prompt and completion text is never stored by the platform; only lengths are.

## Complete a prompt

`POST /v1/ai/complete`

Runs a model completion and returns the text. Pass `jsonSchema` to get JSON that matches a schema.

**Auth:** API token with the ai.complete scope.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/ai/complete" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN" \
  -H "content-type: application/json" \
  --data '{"prompt":"Draft a two-sentence follow-up for quote Q-1042 sent to Example Pty Ltd.","system":"You write short, friendly business emails.","maxTokens":300}'
```

**Request body**

```json
{
  "prompt": "Draft a two-sentence follow-up for quote Q-1042 sent to Example Pty Ltd.",
  "system": "You write short, friendly business emails.",
  "maxTokens": 300
}
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "completion": "Hi Pat, I wanted to check that quote Q-1042 reached you. Let me know if you have any questions.",
  "model": "example-model"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 403 | `ai/forbidden` | `token lacks the ai.complete scope` |
| 400 | `ai/bad-prompt` | `prompt is required (max 40000 chars)` |
| 400 | `ai/bad-system` | `system prompt too long (max 10000 chars)` |
| 429 | `ai/rate-limited` | `hourly completion limit reached` |
| 502 | `ai/failed` | `model call failed; retry later` |
| 400 | `ai/bad-schema` | `jsonSchema was rejected by the model host — schemas are normalised to strict mode (all properties required; use a null type for optional fields), but this one still failed validation` |

`system` and `maxTokens` are optional; `maxTokens` is capped at 2000. `jsonSchema` is `{name, schema}`. When no model is set up the 503 body is a bare `{"error":"no model is configured on this control plane"}` with no code. Limits: 60 completions per hour per caller and 200 per hour per organisation. The 502 is safe to retry; `ai/bad-schema` is not.

<!-- source: https://docs.vmnodes.com/api/organisation.md -->

# Organisation

Incidents record what went wrong and who is handling it. Extensions are third-party apps installed into the organisation; an upgrade that widens access waits for an administrator.

## List extensions

`GET /v1/extensions`

Lists extensions installed in the organisation, with the access each one requested.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/extensions" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "extensionId": "ext_0000000000000000000000000A",
    "name": "visitor-book",
    "publisher": "Example Software",
    "version": "1.2.0",
    "status": "installed",
    "applicationId": "app_00000000000000000000000001",
    "requested": {
      "runtime": {
        "image": "registry.example.com/acme/quotes@sha256:9f2c4a1e7b3d5086a1c2e4f60718293a4b5c6d7e8f90a1b2c3d4e5f60718293a",
        "resources": {
          "cpu": "0.5",
          "memory": "256Mi"
        }
      },
      "publishes": [
        "visits.visit/v1"
      ],
      "consumes": [],
      "actions": [],
      "proposes": [],
      "permissionTemplates": [],
      "mail": {
        "send": false
      },
      "directory": {
        "inviteCustomers": false,
        "lookupPeople": false,
        "listGroupMembers": false
      },
      "ai": {
        "complete": false
      }
    },
    "detail": null
  }
]
```

`requested.runtime.resources` holds optional `cpu`, `memory` and `storage` strings. `status` is the extension's install state.

## List pending upgrades

`GET /v1/extensions/upgrades/pending`

Lists extension upgrades waiting for an administrator. A caller who is not an administrator gets an empty list.

**Auth:** API token.

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/extensions/upgrades/pending" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
[
  {
    "pendingUpgradeId": "pup_01JBX3KS8AVBBFNBP42W5TWSFP",
    "extensionId": "ext_0000000000000000000000000A",
    "extensionName": "visitor-book",
    "fromVersion": "1.2.0",
    "toVersion": "1.3.0",
    "widened": {
      "consumes": [
        "visits.visit"
      ],
      "publishes": [],
      "proposes": [],
      "permissions": [
        "mail.send"
      ],
      "actions": []
    },
    "status": "pending",
    "actionable": true,
    "blockedReason": null,
    "phase": null,
    "detail": null,
    "requestedBy": "usr_00000000000000000000000002",
    "requestedAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
    "decidedAt": null
  }
]
```

`widened` lists only what the upgrade adds, in five lists: `consumes`, `publishes`, `proposes`, `permissions` and `actions`. An upgrade that adds nothing does not wait here. `status` is `pending` while it waits. `actionable` is false, with a `blockedReason`, when the upgrade cannot be approved as it stands.

## Approve an extension upgrade

`POST /v1/extensions/upgrades/{pendingId}/approve`

Approves a pending upgrade and installs it. Approving grants the app new access to the organisation's data, so only an administrator can.

**Auth:** administrator (portal session or API token).

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `pendingId` | path | yes | The pending upgrade id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X POST "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/extensions/upgrades/<pendingId>/approve" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "status": "installed",
  "version": "1.3.0"
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 422 | `extensions/no-pending-upgrade` | `no such pending upgrade` |
| 422 | `extensions/approval-forbidden` | `approving an upgrade needs an organisation administrator, or an admin token. Approving grants an application new access to your data, so it is not a decision any member of the organisation can make.` |

Also returns 422 `extensions/upgrade-decided` when the upgrade was already decided and `extensions/upgrade-partial` when it only partly applied.

## Get extension usage

`GET /v1/extensions/{extId}/usage`

Returns what one extension has consumed: published records, publish runs, action executions, deployments and compute.

**Auth:** API token.

| Parameter | In | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `extId` | path | yes | The extension id. |

**Example**

```bash
curl -sS -X GET "$VMNODES_API_URL/v1/extensions/<extId>/usage" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VMNODES_API_TOKEN"
```

**Response** `200`

```json
{
  "extensionId": "ext_0000000000000000000000000A",
  "name": "visitor-book",
  "status": "installed",
  "reserved": {
    "cpu": "0.5",
    "memory": "256Mi"
  },
  "publishedRecords": 1204,
  "publishRuns": 31,
  "actionExecutions": 8,
  "deployments": 3,
  "computeSampling": {
    "sampledAt": "2026-10-21T22:41:55.000Z",
    "services": [
      {
        "serviceId": "web",
        "status": "running",
        "cpuPercent": 3.2,
        "memoryUsedMiB": 118
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

| Status | Code | Message |
|---|---|---|
| 404 | `api/not-found` | `no such resource` |

`reserved` is what the extension's manifest reserves. `computeSampling` is the latest sample from the host, or the string `not-collected` when none exists.
